I remember finding the devs youtube channel way way back. I remember watching of their videos of this game before for it was even called GTTOD. And I remember when the demo came out.

I played the crap out of that demo when it first came out. It was so simple so nice and concise. a couple of levels the ending door would send you to another random linear one. I loved the fact that the levels in that where linear because you could go faster and faster, like a ball rolling down a hill, learning where each enemy spawns and perfectly tossing grenades to there feet. it was great.

However once the game came out it was a confusing mess, there was a chat? money? perks? what does any of it mean... Even now its still a confusing mess what am I even supposed to do? It plays like a confused mess of titan fall 2, risk of rain, doom and call of duty zombies. so little is told to you the tutorial consists of a couple little missable text boxes that only tell you how to swim, dash and open the orange door... I'm not even sure how to progress. the orange door takes an insane amount of kills to open you need to kill "things" next to it to open it up. BUT it is constantly draining the charge, so that seems like I shouldn't even do that? what the fuck am I supposed to dooooo. Soon you will run out of ammo and have to run around mashing f trying to melee the enemies. which is fun and engaging... All while the threat level increases making more harder enemies spawn...

Just go and get black ops 3 for the zombies, that is literally just a more clear cut version of this. There is even a massive modding scene for it where custom maps are being made with custom weapons, mechanics and enemies.

I wish I was in some alternate universe where this was a linear game with a good progression. Something like doom or doom eternal. Where you start out slow and get faster and get more abilities and fight larger and larger synthwavy monsters... its just really disappointing...

review_text:
Dead by Daylight delivers a level of tension that few multiplayer games can match. Every match raises my heartbeat, especially during chases and loops, and the overall atmosphere consistently keeps me on edge. When the game is running smoothly, the blend of teamwork, stealth, and mind games is genuinely exciting.

The downside is that the experience is highly inconsistent. The game still suffers from frequent bugs, and the presence of hackers can ruin matches outright. New or inexperienced teammates often make the experience frustrating on both sides, whether you queue as killer or survivor. With no in-game communication, coordinating as survivors is challenging, and a single weak link can collapse the entire match structure.

In my experience, about half of the matches feel balanced and enjoyable. The other half are either heavily one-sided or disrupted by teammates who troll, disconnect, or even assist the killer. These situations undermine the competitive tension that makes the game compelling.

On the narrative side, Dead by Daylight has surprisingly rich lore. Some characters have well-developed backstories that add depth to the universe, and exploring that side of the game is a nice bonus for players who enjoy world-building.

Overall, the game offers intense, memorable moments, but the quality of the experience varies significantly from match to match. When it works, it is thrilling. When it doesn’t, it can be genuinely frustrating.

review_text:
I love sniper games and have previously purchased and played sniper ghost warrior 2 and 3. However, I cannot recommend ghost warrior contracts. This is due primarily to the absolutely horrible game saving system. It saves itself at certain intervals, so you have no control over the saves. Worse, however, is the fact that it only saves a single version. You cannot go back to prior saves except the most recent. I spent several hours executing a side mission "bounty". The game saved several times afterward. However upon exiting and restarting the game the bounty mission was still there and I got no credit for finishing it. Apparently I had not left the bounty area even though the game saved. So I then left the bounty area and when I did, the game stated that I had failed the bounty and it disappeared. The only option left for me was to start the entire mission over again loosing many hours of playing time.  This could have been easily remedied by the authors if the game retained even a couple past saved versions. This is inexcusable and demoralizing behavior for a game that makes me want to abandon it. In addition, there is no help feature or directions, so you make a lot of mistakes at first in attempts to learn how things work. Since there is only a single save, you are often screwed on accomplishments like the one previously described. The game was fun otherwise, but because of these horrible mechanics, I simply cannot recommend it.

After playing an additional 33 hours, the game is even worse than I previously described. Perhaps a half dozen times my character gets stuck in limbo on a branch or in between rocks or in the latest case simply backing up to a concrete block. You can't move, jump crouch or use any of your gadgets. The only alternative is to restart, loosing perhaps hours of playing time. Of course, if you could save the game when you want to, you might only loose a few minutes instead. Of the total time I've played, easily half of that is because of  bugs and lack of ability to save. I don't plan on buying another Sniper Ghost Warrior game unless these issues can be demonstrably fixed.

- When modifying your own bike, the career bike will be forced on you as well.
- No server browser, quick match only.
- No quick match filter (will you end up in a standard or pro physics race? Who knows...).
- Etc.

Don't pay full price, it's not worth it! I got this game for 22 euros.

review_text:
Great Sniper game. Feels a bit like sandbox in a way.

+ Fun combat.
+ Non-linear gameplay.
+ Tons of side challenges and side missions.
+ Huge environments.
+ Useful gadgets.
+ You can approach many objectives from multiple angles.
+ You can easily manipulate checkpoints.

- Store prices are too high.
- Less weapons than in Sniper: Ghost Warrior 3.
- More casualised Sniping than it was in Sniper: Ghost Warrior 3. You can see exact wind influence instead of wind blowing direction and speed. Direct combat alse been casualised.
- Enemy A.I. is significantly worse than it was in Sniper: Ghost Warrior 3.
- In later levels, sometimes level design leaves you in huge disadvantages with no cover and hard to see through locations. Sometimes you have nowhere to go or hide and there are enemies on all corners.
- Ammo limits for secondary weapons are absurd.
- Pretty much there isn't a story, actually, there is, but I could barely call it a story. Previous two games had good storylines so here it seems like a downgrade.
- Ending is extremely underwhelming.
- Some very odd glitches. Rarely but a few times enemies teleported about 20 metres away. Once enemy even left a trace, it looked like time was warped like in Quantum Break when you dash. One glitch was hilarious. I threw a flash bang grenade and after it exploded it blew enemy 30 metres into the air, but since it was flash it dealt no damage to him, he then spotted me from the sky flying and while still in mid-air he threw a grenade and killed me...


7/10

1. 영화의 한 주인공 처럼 까진 아니더라도 인게임 보이스로 사람들이랑 트루퍼 놀이 하며 놀 순 있음..
대륙의 그녀석들이 자꾸 중국어로 챗 하는데 깔끔하게 무시하고 영어로 소통 할 수 있으면 하고
가끔 한국인 보면 한국어로 대화해도 재미짐.

2. 클래스 안에 2가지로 나뉘어 져있음
탱커어태커 의 극단적으로 나뉘어져 있는게 아니라서
역할 별로 1인분만 하면 되긴 하는데..
데몰리셔의 폭파 스킬이나 엔지니어의 화염 방사기가 시야를 자꾸 가려서 짜증날 때가 많음.

단점

1. 가끔가다 해커를 만나는게 게임을 완전 망가트림.
전형적인 디펜스 or 전진수비 의 게임모드가 주 를 이루는데
어디서든 핵쟁이 만나면 재미없게 벽뚫 해가며 적을 다 잡아서 경험치도 못얻고
쏘는 재미도 없음. 그냥 게임 한 판 날리는 거라서 클래스 렙업이나 계급 렙업에 치명적임..

2. 내가 하고싶은 맵이랑 게임 모드를 설정 못함.
맵과 모드가 한 번 뜨면 이것들이 유지되는 시간이 있는데
시간이 지나야 맵과 모드가 바뀜.
난 호드 모드를 하고 싶은데 호드 모드가 아예 안뜰때도 있음.

3. 무기
각 클래스 별로 특화된 무기가 1~2개씩 있음
이 무기를 만렙 찍으면 무기고 시스템이 발동되는데
이 무기고 마크가 붙으면 클래스 불문하고 모든 무기를 하나의 클래스에서 사용 가능한데
특정 클래스 레벨이 되어야 됨.
즉, 스나 중 가장 대미지 높은 스나가 Morita XXX 라는 바렛 닮은 스나총이 있는데
13렙인가 부터 사용가능함. 무기고 마크가 붙어도 클래스 레벨이 13렙 되지 않으면 못쓰는데
이 전까진 그냥 기본 무기만 써야됨.
세계관 특성상 무기가 별로 없어서 이해는 한다만... 좀 더 추가됐으면 하는 바람?

4. 매칭
이 게임이 아시아 서버가 있지만 오후엔 평균 3~5분 기다려야 잡히는 경우가 있고
저녁에는 빠릿하게 잡히는데 잘 안잡힌다는 느낌이 많음.
매니아 게임이라서 유저가 한정적인건지 그냥 사람이 없는건지...
매칭이 잘 안잡힌다렙업이 잘 안된다 
로 보면 이해하기 쉬움

공식 파트너로써 지속적으로 건의는 하지만 
디스코드에 있는 Offworld 매니저와 개발자 들이 답변을 ㅈ같이 안해줌.
23년 10월에 건의 했던 내용의 답장을 안하는 편.
파트너 전용 디코에 올려도 답을 다른 파트너가 해주니
테스트는 유저한테 시키고 그걸 토대로 피드백 받아서 업데이트를 하다보니
좀 말이 안되게 업뎃이 될 수도있으니 참고하시길..

But its a scam to ask 50 dollars for this game, as it greets you with performance issue after performance issue, bugs, and optimization problems. Every update seems to make this game weaker and weaker. 

SST needs some serious quality of life updates before putting out anymore content... 

Bumping your game up 20 dollars along with the issue of bugs, but throwing more content on top of it to mask it? Thats a real power play from Offworld. 

There's no way I can recommend this game for 50 dollars, consider waiting for a sale or until devman can get their shit together.

review_text:
It's so much worse than I thought. It's mechanically threadbare, it's cheap difficulty (relying way too much on unavoidable head traps), characterisation is dog-shit, writing is banal and ham-fisted, and it's just so fucking boring. The guns lack impact, the upgrades are meh, the combat requires no skill or tactics at all you can get away with button mashing, it pulls a hard 180 on one character out of fucking nowhere in an attempt at unearned pathos. The story beats are so telegraphed if you've played any sci-fi game, read any sci-fi book, or watched any fucking episode of The X-Files. It's just horrendous.

The ONLY positives are that it looks pretty decent, and is decently optimised. As a horror game though, it fucking fails. There's maybe one good jump-scare in it, but it barely even clears that fucking bar and even that one is so fucking telegraphed you have to be thick to miss it. 

What a garbage experience. Only recommend if you want a legit turn-your-brain-off experience that does absolutely nothing of worth.

review_text:
The combat and movement feel sluggish, attacks have a long windup, most stair cases in the game are wider than needed so you can miss the jump up them if you are not paying enough attention.
Combat lethality is high, you may get comboed from full health to dead if you are in a bad position, this can even happen against non boss enemies. I did kill 2 of the bosses on my first try due to good weapon combinations.

review_text:
I really wanted to like this game, but after playing for a while I felt like I had to take a step back and stop. I enjoyed myself for the first few seasons, but there were a couple things that I started noticing that hampered my enjoyment.

Gonna start with the things that I genuinely really like about this game because it does have a lot going for it. First off, the art style. It's really cute and reminds me of Paper Mario in the best way (which I think might be intentional given how close the two art styles are). Everyone looks great and I enjoy walking around town because it looks amazing. I also really like the level of customization that you have available to you, as one of my favorite things to do in game was run to the tailor and see what stuff I could get to customize my character. I also reaaaaaaaally appreciate things not being gender locked, one of my least favorite things is having things locked because I didn't decide to play a particular gender character, and having everything be the same regardless of my character's gender was something I really appreciated. I also like how the town always feels like its changing, whether that be through characters dying or being born, or travelers coming in for the town fair. That's all I can think of for now but I do think there's a lot more that's good about this game, but now I'm gonna discuss my main issues with the game.

First of all, I do want to clarify that having the possibility of your fellow town members dying is genuinely really cool. That being said, within the first in game week my entire town caught a disease and the vast majority of them died. The first funeral you go to is really impactful, but then it loses almost all meaning once you have one quite literally every day for several weeks (I think I had like, 10+ in a row at LEAST). Also, all of the carpenters died so I couldn't get any buildings for several days which really sucked (There was a replacement carpenter to replace the starting ones but she also died lol). The death thing is really neat but it just happens way too often to feel impactful, diseases are insane and if one pops up say goodbye to literally everyone you know because barely anyone is surviving that unless you intervene (which wasn't a thing to my knowledge when this happened).

Another issue I had is that you don't have many options for how to spend your time each day. After you water all your crops, you're pretty much limited to fishing, talking to NPCs, or going around clicking every interactable item on the map to get more materials. It's fun at first but quickly gets pretty boring (I'm at winter right now). Maybe it's because I tend to play games for really extended periods of time (like several hours at a time) and I got burned out, but I do feel like I'm doing the same exact thing over and over again. Additionally, all the things to do feel really similar to each other, so I feel like all I'm doing is running around the map collecting stuff, going to bed, then repeating. Just feels like busywork, and I know farming sim games are just kinda like that sometimes but this is the only game so far in the genre where I've felt this issue, and I think it's just due to the lack of variety of activities to fill in the time, they all feel really similar to each other.

Also, I think the final thing is that crops feel really unbalanced. I know this is a casual game, but the multi-harvest plants are so much better than anything else that it feels unfair. From my experience, every crop sells for the same amount, but some of them can get harvested multiple times AND give more than one crop every harvest, while some can only be harvested once and give you one crop. Maybe this got changed since I stopped playing but I was looking through the patch notes and I didn't see anything. Just felt pointless to buy 90% of the seeds when there was a very clear best option. The literal only reason I would plant some of these is if I were trying to make a specific recipe which just doesn't feel good to me.

All that being said, I do think this game is fun for the first several hours. I think the primary issue is that the game doesn't feel like it evolves ever. I got married and had kids but it felt like nothing really changed. Everyone takes ages to grow up even when you set the growth speed to fast and I just felt like all I was doing was waiting for everyone to grow older instead of feeling like I'm making progress. I think if you're not going to play this for very long, it's a good time, but I struggled to want to play this game long term.

5. 20 player co-op contains objectives but NO ONE will perform the objective that does not require killing. If you expect to accomplish the objective by holding down the interact button...DO NOT EXPECT ANYONE TO DO IT!!!!!!!!!!  NO ONE WILL!!!! TRUST ME! Instead they would rather defend you and kill as much as possible why?  HERE IS WHY!!!!!  BECAUSE YOU GET MVP for BEING THE TOP DAMAGE DEALER!!!!!!!!  YOU READ THAT CORRECTLY---- DAMAGE DEALER, MVP within a hold this interact button to win.    YOU'VE DONE IT SONIC THE HEDGE HOG DESIGNER -- You really made it work! You got Sonic running around, and you got Tails holding the button.... but TAILS is never MVP because Knuckles is killing everyone and sonic just keeps on RUNNING!

6. Free Roam... yea okay.. The sonic designer man strikes yet again.  The Free ROAM.... hahah THE FREE ROAM........ yo the FREE ROAM HAS 5 ENEMIES PER MILE!!!!!!!!!! Yup. YOU RUN and RUN and RUN just to find 1  monster.  You are Sonic the hedge hog basically. 

7. "Good Job Sonic the Hedge Hog Man-- You've done it." x infinity.

Kinda strange how more than half the cast of characters are female, and more than 90% of unlocks are female only cosmetics. Good job sonic man, you really tried to make a female sonic.

Perhaps its Fortnite inspired seasons with a meteorite about to crash into the map that took ages to arrive. Maybe some unknown Dr. Strange character is going to introduce the multiverse in some manner; I really dont know.  Its just SOOOOO EMPTY right now!!!!!!! But why?!  Please tell us Sonic the hedge hog man! 

10. "Good Job Sonic the Hedge Hog Man-- You've done it." x infinity + 1 more.

review_text:
As a game: no.
As a work of art: yes.

To elaborate, all the "video game parts" of Scorn are pretty bad. Especially the combat. I think this game would have been far better with zero combat and instead all that dev time could have been focused on the "immersion in an alien world" part of the experience. Most of the puzzles are pretty meh as well. There's really no discernible story as well, which was on purpose? More on that in a moment. 

As a piece of art it's pretty good. It's weird (not weird enough though, in my opinion), and very alien. It's so alien that nothing makes sense and it's almost [i]alienating[/i], which I still can't decide if that is good or bad. Clearly the alien nature of the game is the point, but the alien nature of everything makes it a difficult experience to interact with, and I think they should have leaned into that far more. Ditch the combat and traditional puzzles and have the experience be all about trial and error figuring out how to navigate a totally alien environment. I think that would have made an amazing experience.

Additional thoughts: clearly a lot of effort when into this game. Near the end of the game when you are [spoiler]using the baby crusher to make the red baby juice, and you crush three babies, each crushing animation is unique! That's great! I love that detail.[/spoiler] But in other aspects there was not nearly as much regard, like when you shoot your gun you don't actually pull the trigger! There is no animation for pulling the trigger. And don't tell me the gun is shot via some other interaction like a neural link or whatever, because if that was the case then there should not have been a trigger on the gun in the first place. Just another small example why there should have been zero combat.

Lastly, there is penis in the game one time, and it does involve a penis sucking device. It's great. I love it. H.R. Giger would surely be proud. However! It is only one time. There should have been more. Legit, a lot of panel triggers involve sticking individual fingers into holes to activate elevators and things. Should have just been penis holes triggered by penis insertion. That would have been rad.

review_text:
Better than expected, much more engaging than Arizona Sunshine. Feels like "The Division" in VR. I like that it offers multiple difficulty levels allowing me to play casual & explore the environment. I can always increase the difficulty level if I choose to be challenged down the line. 

I picked up the Deluxe Edition on sale & the game appears to be polished. Plays fine with the HP Reverb G2 WMR headset & the motion controllers. The gun-play is simplistic but very satisfying.  Even playing with pistols is fun, especially if you upgrade it & get a little more fire power. The fastest way to earn capital is to play at higher difficulty levels to gain greater rewards.  It's best to team up with online players whom have better weapons & can help you complete the missions.

The zombies are not that scary but you can get some good jump scares if you're not careful around corners or if they jump down on you from the ceiling. Based on initial impression, I would recommend it. It's different enough from other 3rd party shooters to warrant a purchase. Feels like I'm at a theme park having a fun shoot um up experience.

You can play solo with bots or online multi-player. Haven't had any issues with multi-player which is quite fun. Being able to play with bots ensures you can always play without worrying about a lack of players. This allows you to improve your skill set, build your capital, acquire new weapons and obtain new weapon upgrades.

This has turned out to become one of my favorite VR games. It's not perfect when it comes to the stick controls but it's a minor inconvenience which doesn't really impact the overall experience. It's fun and immersive especially when you upgrade your weapons & can team up with others to battle online.


##############


So I've taken advantage of the weekend & played a few times throughout Friday, Saturday & Sunday. I've managed to acquire just about all the weapons available playing casual off and online. Offline I played the easiest mode to just relax but online I mostly play the hardest levels. Once you pass the 20 hr mark or so it gets repetitive so to keep it fresh it will be best to upgrade your weapons, mix & match, play with friends or strangers online & not play daily. 

It's fun but because you might be playing online, you will most likely being playing the same maps often unless you are the leader & invite players to the maps you want to play. With that said, there are some glitches at times but it shouldn't ruin the fun all that much. You can always host your own game or play solo in some maps to avoid anyone whom may be wasting your time glitching the vending arcade cabinets.

review_text:
One of the worst Games of the Current gaming era. The controls are clunky at the best of times. Most of the time the most important controls bug out "Mantling" over obstacles or climbing terrain and crouching under obstacles only for your character to not move or respond to direction inputs. The game more than once bugged out and wouldn't progress the quest line until you leave the area and re-enter it only then does the npc's tell you "you need to get the key from one of the guards" even though it was already painfully obvious as you had done this multiple times before... only to progress further you had to "trigger" the dialogue que to continue. The worst part was the terribly clunky combat that didn't work half of the time and when it did you would get swarmed by 5-10 mobs in certain areas. Achievements are bugged. I upgraded 2 weapons to max and  I only got the achievement for fully upgrading a weapon in the dlc mission "Final Transmission". 

The story was Average at best and terrible at worst. This was because, the gameplay was mostly a walking simulator with very typical jump scares, and combat which was supposed to be one of the main advantages of the game sucked. A fully upgraded shotgun took 3-5 shots to kill a "space Zombie" while my melee stun baton (More like club) as my character refused to use it's electrical options, took only 3-7 swings depending on the type of mob, making most ammunition worthless to keep and on the few bosses that appeared in the game the damage was god awful for the guns again. 

The reason i believe the combat was so bad was that the guns did barely any damage, you were swarmed by lots of space zombies often, and the main replay loop of the combat was press 'a' or 'd' to dodge damage when you tried to use 's' to block damage you get grabbed alot or swarmed by another space zombie further making gunplay feel bad. 

If you are on the fence about buying Callisto Protocol, do know that some of the developers that worked on dead space contributed to this game, and it did not help. Skip Callisto Protocol and buy Deadspace. This game its a "cheap" and "mediocre" game that tried and failed horribly at reproducing the great enjoyment and fear that deadspace had. 



Story 4-10 |      Decent enough, but far to easy to understand and i figured out the entire story when i saw the cargo container box in the tutorial mission.     
Weather effects 7-10 |    The snowy chapter was fun but you only saw these affects for that one mission.
Sound 6-10 |      (eery sounds effects which added to the atmosphere but most of the sound instantly notified you where the enemies were going to come from in advance, took away from the horror aspect greatly.)
Lighting 5-10 |      (Some times your guns flashlight didnt even work even through it did before you saved and exited the game.)

As for Final Transmission DLC: Just some of the worst content to play says you get to use your completed saved game data to keep your weapons... You dont, i lost all upgrades and most of my weapons except for my shotgun and pistol. The Powerhammer should have been in base game would have made much more sense and been more fun. The final boss of the DLC was terrible to fight did lots of teleporting and then would just spam fire Aoe explosives at you knocking you down then running at you to kill you, was infuriating. Darksouls, Eldenring and any other tough game had much better controls for fun and difficult boss fights, not just spam and kill. 

Overall rating I would give 3-10.

I don't generally experience this as I was one of the original players with a lifetime subscription so when they went free to play this was changed to grant players like me a monthly stipend. So when I do go back to playing I'm generally stupid rich across the board.

I just wish someone would come around with a hybrid Star Trek Bridge Commander and Star Trek Elite force.

review_text:
TL;DR: Overall, I am loving the game so far. It has flaws and hopefully sees some post launch support but its my favorite modern MX game.

I see a lot of negative reviews and while the game deserves critisism I think a lot of it is exagurated and people are giving impressions on a stock bike without doing the rider training. NOTE: Do the rider training! I didnt realize it was worth doing but it improves your rider in a number of ways which is a bit silly to hide that fact.

Ill address the common complaints and throw in my $.02

-Performance/graphics: I'm running a modern i5, SSD, 16gb RAM and 970 GTX. At 1080p with everything on max except bloom and motion blur I get a solid 60 fps on most tracks and 50 in the compound. I do not get the stuttering that it seems some people are getting, maybe I'm just lucky. The game looks great. Seeing the "ruts" fill up with water is pretty cool although it is a bit overdone and looks like you are just riding in a river by the end of the race. There is a distinct lack of water effects from riding through it on the track but its not nearly as bad as MX vs ATV All Out. My main complaint for the graphics is your back tire. It doesn't really appear to spin or change speeds apart from going and stop. There is particle effects kicked up from other bikes but your back tire appears lifeless

-AI: Is pretty mindless. They have one line in which they take and that is pretty well the extent of it. If you are in the way of that line they will crash into you

-Ruts and berms: The track deformation does affect gameplay however not really in a way I had hoped. The track gets beat up but really all it does is make it rougher and easier to go down but true ruts are never formed. However, even if they were, you would just slide out of them which leads into:

-Handling: I really enjoy the handling of the game (have only played on PRO). If you have played previous MXGP games you have a pretty good idea of what you are getting into. The back end slides out a bit more than I feel it should but its not nearly as bad as people are making it out to be. Again, put some better tires on your bike, do the training and its entirely different from when you first start up the game. You need to feather the throttle a bit to keep traction coming out of turns.

As far as the crashing on overjumps I see a lot of people saying its overdone however when I have watched gameplay of people complaining about it they are usually landing hard on their back wheel and wondering why they crash. I have crashed on a couple overjumps I felt as though I shouldn't have, used rewind and made sure I landed proper and rode away without a crash. No issue from me here.

My main complaint is the berms and how far over you can lean the bike before crashing. Some tracks have a hard, sharp berm on the outside corner. You should be able to lean the bike over and rail the corner. Instead you will either just blow over the top edge or crash from leaning over too hard. Apart from that I really enjoy the handling of the bikes.

Air Control: Again, do the training, it improves your air control and scrubs. Whips and scrubs, pretty well same as all the other MXGP games but a little bit better. Free in the sense that you can go as far as you want with them but not free like MX vs ATV games. The scrubs work pretty good to keep you low if you carve the face of the jump right but it wont let you do a Bubba scrub due to crashing from leaning over too hard. The air control is still fairly stiff but I feel as though its better than any previous MXGP games (note: I didnt play 3). I don't care about whips so I do not mind the air control although it could be improved

Sound: You're best off just watching a couple youtube videos if you are picky about the sound. Its passable to me.

Tracks: Same affair as previous games. Youre getting licenced tracks for better or worse. Personally, I don't like a lot of the tracks and I am hoping for some more North American style tracks down the road. The compound is pretty good.

Customization: Its gonna be a grind if you want to spruce up you're bike and rider. I don't really care about much of that apart from throwing the best components on my bike but there seems to be a pretty good deal of options to choose from if thats your thing.

review_text:
Just Cause 4 should have been the sandbox to end all sandboxes. The franchise itself represented a departure from the usual rules of the open world sandbox by allowing the players un-parallelled mobility, and Just Cause 3 took this player mobility to it's logical conclusion as well as abandoning any pretense of trying to gate keep the player's power level behind contrived obstacles.

Just Cause 4 was a day one purchase for me. I was a huge fan of the franchise when it existed, and within an hour of firing it up I had already rage quit and didn't touch it again for 6 years. 

Where did it all go wrong? There's a whole story here about the closure of Avalanche New York, private investment, tax policy, greed, and art for profit's sake, but rather than marinating on the game we should have played, lets talk about the one we got:

Solis is beautiful, but dead compared to JC3s Medici and especially JC2's Panay... there is actually quite a lot of character to the world and some incredible location design... but the game only bothers to engage you with it once. The story missions, strikes, etc never start to feel like an organic part of the world around you. Just Cause 4's challenges never rise above the level of menial nonsense. Everything just feels like it was pasted into the world. Did you find a light house? You bet your sweet bippy there's gonna a wing suit challenge where you have to flop lazily to the ground through the exact same three rings as the other twenty lighthouses pasted along the shore. There's something to the order of 300 such challenges the game asks you to complete, but if I had to guess I would say there are actually fewer  than 30 unique challenges and the rest is just "That other challenge, but over here now."

A not-insignificant portion of the game just... literally does not work. Stunt ramps are placed against oncoming traffic, which in itself would not be a problem except for the algorithm the game uses to populate the world around you. The game will ALWAYS draw a car at a position relative to your location to keep the world busy. In the event of oncoming traffic, this system then works with the NPCs self-preservation, to guarantee that on five out of five approaches to a poorly placed ramp, an NPC in the oncoming traffic lane will ALWAYS stop between the player and the ramp. 

So you start problem solving. Maybe if you block traffic, you think, that will solve the problem. But it never does. Now imagine spending multiple minutes/attempts/deaths trying to get just ONE of what should be some of the easiest stunts in the game, and when you finally manage to set it up so that you can actually hit the ramp, it dead-stops your vehicle killing you instantly because the stunt ramp was never set up at an appropriate level to the ground in the first place or the developers just never bothered to check if the vehicle they assigned to that challenge had the wheel clearance to actually use the ramp they placed. 

At the highest level, you really only have two or three attempts at any given task before the background noise of freedom fighters, Blackhand soldiers, panicked bystanders, and exploding combinations of all three makes success, if not survival, an impossibility. A cascade of small annoyances quickly gather strength into an Avalanche of bullshit. The faster you learn to never trust the developers or their intended solutions to any of the missions or puzzles in the game, the happier you are bound to be. 

Every Strike mission in the game relies on an infinite supply of enemies to make the challenge. Most of the times this doesn't make much of a difference... but on a few select missions the game decides to add another infinite supply of enemies which quickly breaks the game. 

Sargento's storyline culminates in a mission called Beachhead that mandates you be pursued by two gunship helicopters at all times. It also mandates that you sink several large warships. The type of ammunition that you need to handle both of these tasks is finite, and if you're at all clever you quickly see where that mission becomes a seriously un-fun slog. Even if you luck out and are able to tether the two gunships together before they can start making your life difficult, two more instantly spawn. I don't mean, "two more will eventually show up." I mean, two new helicopters will INSTANTLY spawn behind you. They will already be targeting you before the last two chassis hit the ground.

Negotiating enemy escalation with the AI in this game honestly feels like arguing with someone who is too committed to admit they were wrong. On a fairly regular basis, the game will just forget that the enemy is supposed to stop looking for you after a while. Like when you're grappled to the top of a cave, in the middle of nowhere, with no enemy soldiers around for kilometers. 

Like before, this would just be a minor annoyance by itself... by the time you have boosters and air lifters dealing with most enemy units is facile. But after a long enough time being hunted, the game seems to decide that the only way to deescalate is to just kill you outright. Enemy air units will literally start to kamikaze you with a predictability that would make Darth Bob blush. The combination of these two factors does occasionally result in hilarity, like when you spend ten minutes grappled to the ceiling of said cave just to listen to the game endlessly call in air support only for the Blackhand jets to explode trying to fly through the mountain to reach you.

If you're a huge fan of capture & control game play and sandbox games, you can probably squeeze enough blood out of this stone to make it worth a deeply discounted purchase. However, if you're a die-hard fan of the franchise who just finished 3 and is hoping for the next big blow-out... keep looking.

review_text:
This game is certainly promising however I would not recommend the game in it's current state. Whilst it is fun for some time and has many items and craftables, the dialogue gets very stale after just a few hours. It's a great pity because the whole dynasty feature is cool but I can't find myself feeling attached to characters who mutter the same lines over and over again. There are personalities but they often feel samey with just a few outliers. Interestingly to the game's credit, they do influence the quests that specific personality of villager will give you.

I would say my next biggest complaint is likely the mines too or lack of. It is very rudimentary with it just consisting of a few tunnels you wander through. You make your way through to the end of the tunnels to mine some ore or gems then rinse and repeat the next day. It ends up feeling like a chore you only really do because its a decent way to earn some money.Again, there's no procedural generation or anything literally just a few straight paths....

This game simply doesn't feel like a full release which it claims to be. Whilst there is still a lot of fun to be had, I would wait on this one.

review_text:
Stunning visuals (especially for 2007) with a unique theme that combines 1950s culture with 19th century fascination with underwater exploration using contemporary industrial technology (a la 10000 Leagues under the Sea). The world is immersive, and the dark, grimy, aquatic and industrial atmosphere add to the claustrophobic effects that you truly have no idea what crazed maniac is around the corner. The enemy design and dialogue fit the story and horror themes very well.

Regarding the story and level design, the first half was excellent, with Fort Frolic being the peak of how engaging the game could be for the 2 hours you run around this abandoned entertainment district. The 2nd half lost the momentum and magic, with no bosses or enthralling plot points (after the plot twist), and it felt like running around the map.

I played on Normal difficulty and found it too difficult in the middle of the game, where you constantly run out of ammo and eve, and the shotgun Big Daddy can kill you in 2 shots. The 2nd half got gradually easier and easier, where by the end, I barely ever ran out of eve, health, or ammo, no new enemies were introduced, and I had overpowered weapons, plasmids, and upgraded slots.

There's also the stupid pipe puzzle in the game. It's fun the first few times, until you realize you'd have to repeat it every few minutes if you want those small discounts, which I realized isn't even necessary since I kept reaching the money cap. It was so repetitive and frustrating, especially when half the time, the puzzles were literally impossible. Once you get to the 2nd half of the game, you should have more than enough upgraded slots to remove most of the overload and alarm tiles to very easily knock them out of the way.

review_text:
You’re returning to the place you grew up in only to find out it is not your home anymore. Instead, it rejects you like a foreign organ, forcing you into a life on the periphery, on the outside looking into a place where your birthright once was to belong. What happened? You realize the tethers to this life are worn and some have snapped already in your absence. Do you mend the broken strings or weave anew with threads you’ve once ignored? 
To me, Pathologic is about perseverance in the face of grief (or Grief, hehe), about continuing to fight despite everything and everyone you have lost already. It’s about bloodily carving a place for yourself in a community that rejects you, about the ways people love and the ways that love eats them up from the inside out. It’s about how sometimes life gives you no winning options and all you can do is Lose A Little Less Bad and in that, it forces you to reevaluate what it even means to lose. 
On my first playthrough, I restarted after I lost my first character. On my second playthrough, I lost them again. I was going to start over but I reached out to a friend who told me that I had to face it and get through it. Better luck next time. He was right. I found a way I could have saved them a few in-game days later. Had I not continued despite my (genuine!) sadness at their passing, I would’ve never gotten much further. 
I believe the reason the game wants you to fail (and you know it does, you’ve probably watched the hbomberguy video just the same as me) is not primarily to make you suffer along with your character. I think it’s about showing you that you can and will keep going despite it. This game doesn’t want your frustration, it wants your defiance. It wants you to look at all the hours you’ve already wasted walking through God’s Most Depressing Russian Town, all the health and items you’ve already lost, all the people you’ve already lost and go “I don’t care. Because there is something left for me here and that something, as little as it is, is worth fighting for”. 
Now here’s the thing about this humble reviewer specifically: I’m soft. I can’t kill people in video games because it makes me feel bad, I cry when people are mean to pigeons and were I not a little intellectually understimulated by games that don’t make me suffer a little you’d probably find me in the animal crossing review section ONLY. And I’m pretty sure that’s the only reason the game worked so well for me. You need to be willing to connect to this game on a visceral level, you need to be willing to feel for the fake people in your computer. I need you to play this one with your heart. Otherwise it’s just a weird game about being bad at hitting.

They’re composed of earthly materials that are structured in a way that produces a uniquely ‘extraterrestrial’ feel for all the games’ backdrops. Samorost 2 is decently fun as a point-n-click game, but I’d wager that visuals are what brings in and occupies the large majority of players. Putting aside the game’s art (and the splendid soundtrack) that carries much of the experience, the pace of puzzles grinds to a halt on too many occasions for such a compact game. I wish it were easier to tell which elements can be clicked on as well as which elements are important or need to be dragged instead of clicked. Regardless, Samorost 2 is a fine distraction given its generous sales price, and it’s probably worth having if you're an adamant fan of Amanita's work.

review_text:
Having put over 150 hours into this game at the time of writing, I can confidently say that it has held my attention far better than other coop horde shooters in recent years. I keep coming back to ST:E long after having lost interest in Helldivers 2 and Space Marine 2. The only games in it's genre that I have put more time into are World War Z and Aliens Fireteam, both games I have had far longer. ST:E feels very similar to the latter 2 games of that comparison and I can fully recommend it to anyone who enjoyed either of those equally excellent games.

The game consists of a very basic gameplay loop for the most part, building a base and defending it from waves of bugs, or defending an objective under similar circumstances. Its an extremely fun and addicting gameplay system that doesn't get boring even after hundreds of hours! The class system has, over time, become much more expansive. This means they now all feel a lot more unique and contribute to a more dynamic gameplay feel when cooperating with other players. The game also has an incredible soundtrack that perfectly invokes the feeling of the original Poledouris score while maintaining its own identity.

The games biggest flaw is its performance. The game launched in early access in 2023 and still suffers from significant slow down, frame drops, and pop in even on high end rigs. Connection issues are abundant too and often seem entirely random and can result in being kicked from matches. Something that is a huge inconvenience when matches often take over 30 minutes. There are also a list of bugs that can occur from time to time and you will likely come across at least one in every match you play.

The game is one of the most fun shooters I have played in years and it is on that basis that I can recommend the game wholeheartedly. However, those without a tolerance for the performance issues and bugs would be more than justified in avoiding this title, especially as it  has now officially released for full price. A move which is very disappointing given its current state. I would urge anyone that is interested in the game, but hesitant about buying it, to check back regularly as the game continues to be patched.

I've played this game for 2000+ hours and I must say for a simulation game, it does what it's supposed to do - simulate. This is a game I let run in the background once I've built up my team, which is something I really like doing with any simulation game. What I thought is cool about this game is that , the stats do matter and will effect your team, the front office you have also effects your team too. This game is really detailed when it comes to what actually effects your team and how the simulation runs. Sometimes, even if you build up this monster, stacked forward team, but lack depth, experienced defence and a reliable goalie, your team won't simlate as you expect - which is really nice. On top of all this, experience does play a HUGE factor when it comes to simulating and playoffs. If you run with a team that is all rookies, your team will not simulate well because they don't have experience nor do they have experienced players around them. That goes with the playoffs too, if your team is inexperienced in the playoffs you won't go deep until your players gain enough experience. 

I think the only negative I see are is the salary cap does not move. But it can be raised video EHM Assistant, which does wonders if you want to raise salary cap like the real NHL. Otherwise, amazing game would recommend!

review_text:
Somewhere between a tower defense game and a village sim. Manage your growing economy, create a maze of towers and walls to funnel zombie attacks into kill zones, and gradually meet the needs of your burgeoning town. Eventually, hopefully, wipe out the corruption and migrate to a new map.

What makes it really fun is that every failure counts towards something. The main way to play the game is on the world map, where you pick a region to start in. Performing actions in that region accrues god points, which you spend on randomized perks that apply to ALL regions. Even if you fail and have to doom your town because you goofed your build order (a common occurrence), you're still making gradual, tangible progress. Your villagers get a little strong, your towers hit a little harder, you build houses a little faster, and so on.

Big fan of the art style as well. The pixel art on the structures is wonderfully detailed, and all the chirps and grunts of the villagers reminds me of Settlers 2, one of my favorite games of all time.

A hidden gem. Shame the developer is a bit of a conservative crank on Twitter and incapable of keeping his promise of regular updates. It's fully-featured as-is, at least.

review_text:
Yakuza 5 expands on the multi-protagonist approach of its predecessor, this time featuring five playable characters: Kiryu, Saejima, Akiyama, Haruka, and Shinada. Each character has their own storyline, which eventually ties into the bigger picture. 

Story:

The narrative takes some questionable turns. Kiryu leaving the orphanage felt out of character, even if it was "necessary," and his stint as a taxi driver didn’t really suit him. Saejima’s story starts off with another prison sequence (which felt like a rehash of Yakuza 4), but his survival story in the mountains was fantastic—I wish they had focused more on that instead.

Haruka’s storyline, which introduces her as a playable character, was a fresh idea but could have been done better. Akiyama, unfortunately, felt like an afterthought. Shinada, on the other hand, had the strongest arc, with an interesting baseball backstory that connected well with Dojima.

The finale had a few twists—Kurosawa being the Omi chairman instead of a detective was decent, and Aizawa being his son. But overall, the villains felt underwhelming, and the story didn't live up to its full potential. Especially compared to say Yakuza 2 and 3.

Gameplay:
Combat remains largely unchanged from Yakuza 4. Each character has their own strengths—Kiryu and Saejima are the powerhouses, Akiyama is fast, and Shinada relies on weapons. Regular enemies are easy, even on Legend difficulty, but the coliseum is another story.

The coliseum fights are tedious, with enemies blocking almost everything, having multiple health bars, and  reducing your heat action damage. Instead of being challenging, they’re just drawn-out and grindy. Some characters, like Kiryu and Saejima, can exploit certain moves to win, while Shinada struggles because he isn’t built for these fights and you can't even use weapons with him. The rewards aren’t worth the effort unless you're aiming for 100% completion. 

Side Content:
The side jobs were some of the best parts of the game. Kiryu’s taxi missions were surprisingly fun, and Saejima’s hunting segments were excellent, they should have focused his story more on that. Haruka’s idol career was interesting (even if repetitive) and something new for the series. Akiyama, unfortunately, had no job-related activities, while Shinada’s baseball minigames fit his character well. 

Minigames are the usual mix of returning and new activities. The worst one remains fishing—river fishing is okay, but sea fishing is pure frustration, thanks to the constant fishing of steel barrels. Casino and card games are trivialized by cheat items, while SEGA games are only challenging until you figure out their exploits. On the bright side, the UFO catcher was the easiest in the series—finally, no frustration there.

Bugs:
I encountered a few technical issues. The game occasionally froze when getting a weapon revelation, which made me stop doing them altogether (not that they were worthwhile). Another annoyance was the prize ticket system—despite having a “good day” status, I kept getting pocket tissues, forcing me to reload 12 times just to get a pearl. The gacha mechanics in this game were frustrating, and I hope they removed them in later entries. The game is supposed to be fun not a chore.

Conclusion
Despite its flaws, Yakuza 5 is still a great game, as my 150+ hours prove. However, it could have been better with a tighter story, improved combat balancing, and fewer grindy elements. If you're a Yakuza fan, it's worth playing, but be prepared for some frustrating moments along the way.

Rating: 7.5/10

review_text:
Not going to recommend this game, and will request a refund, for the simple reason that I did not find it fun. 

As others have stated, there are many abilities that could easily be shared by different characters, but aren't, in order to artificially limit player choice. 

For example: 
[list]
[*] The Samurai can heave a heavy barrel onto a roof, but not throw a pebble to distract his enemies. 
[*] The ninja assassin only has [i]one[/i] shuriken.
[*]  The ninja  assassin has exactly [b]zero[/b] decoys, but the samurai does.
[/list]

Makes sense. Now, if any character could do anything, then they'd be boring and interchangeable. However, some overlap should still exist. In games like XCOM, this is dealt with in a more sensical fashion: almost anyone can throw a grenade, but some will not be accurate, or not have much range. That approach is far superior.

What really got me is that the only way that the game becomes a little more interesting is by trying to complete both general, and mission specific challenges, not the objectives. For example, there's one challenge that states that you should kill no one other than the target in any given mission.That makes it difficult to complete a level, for sure. Maybe impossible for some, idk as I haven't played enough. But having to artificially limiting my own actions in order to make the game more interesting, is a sign of poor design. 

Another thing that bothered me is the terrible camera control. It's difficult to grasp all the different paths to an objective without rotating the camera [b]often[/b], and having to press ALT, while also switching characters, etc. is annoying. Add the contextual actions (CTRL + Click to drop a body in a bush), and it gets annoying. 

One more I'll add is that the character AI is pretty dumb. Often, if you tell them to reach a certain point, and they have to say, go through a door to get there, or jump down a ledge, they won't perform the action without your explicit instructions. Makes ferrying the team over to a given spot an annoying chore.

At the end of the day, this game simply did not "spark joy". Playing it felt vaguely chore-like.

review_text:
This game simply reeks of "Dev Crunch". There was a very obvious attempt at making a genuinely enjoyable experience, holding the Dead Space franchise as a pedestal for its expected success... Sadly, there are a lot of moments in this game that make me doubt "Was there supposed to be a mechanic here?" Or incredibly frustrating gameplay elements that seemingly Ignored their source material for no apparent reason.

A lot of the issues with this game stem from the fact that... Modern Game Development requires developers to Heavily cut down on Ideas, Experimentation, and Creativity. With a lot of this game's playtime being spent in boring moments where the main character is slowed down by... Goop on the floor, Crawling through Vents, Shimmying through gaps, Waiting for blind enemies to turn their backs to you, etc.

In its DLC, they introduced "Puzzles"...  those of which only 3 exist in the entire DLC... but they feel as if they were meant to be introduced within the Main Game, as "Fixing Electronics" Puzzles were an essential part of Dead Space (the game of which Callisto Protocol was based on)

There are several other instances of interactions feeling Hollow, like something was Meant to be there, but was just... silently removed by the Developers. The incredible amount of Padding serving as its main way to increase how long the players will have to endure before they finish the game.

Most notably of all... This game is extremely easy, it holds your hand throughout every second. Even Combat!

review_text:
Pros
The combat feels excellent, with highly satisfying visuals, impactful camera work, and impressive bullet effects.
The game environment is stunning, making exploration enjoyable.
The Gacha equipment system adds an exciting layer of progression.
Each weapon has unique effects, creating diverse and interesting gameplay styles.
I appreciate mechanics that punish mistakes, like the calamity bar increasing when taking risks or making errors—it adds an extra layer of challenge.
Overall, the game is solid, and I plan to keep playing.
Cons
The price feels too steep for the amount of content available. After 15 hours, I’ve completed all three levels and earned 17 out of 20 achievements. The game needs significantly more content to justify its cost.
The stamina system is overly punishing. Losing large amounts of stamina when hit makes later levels frustrating since you get hit frequently. Stamina is required for everything except walking, so escaping enemies becomes nearly impossible once you run out. You're left with two options: "spray and pray" or slowly walk away, hoping to survive. Worse, shooting and jumping prevent stamina regeneration, making the system feel overly restrictive. This is easily my least favourite mechanic in the game—it creates a frustrating loop that feels unfair rather than challenging.
While the visuals are excellent, they have a very distinct UE5 look. This isn’t necessarily bad, but as more games adopt this style, it starts feeling less unique. I prefer a more distinctive art direction.
Conclusion
Right now, I can’t recommend the game, mainly due to its high price relative to the content. The gameplay loop is enjoyable, but with such limited content, it becomes repetitive quickly—at least for me. If the game receives more content in the future, I might reconsider, but as it stands, it doesn’t feel like it offers enough value for the cost.

review_text:
[h1] Get this and then get OpenRCT2 [/h1]

Roller Coaster Tycoon 1 & 2 are among the greatest games of all time. They are still just as fun today as they were when I played them as a kid, and you will not regret buying them today. That being said, they [i]can[/i] be improved. RCT 2 has lackluster scenarios compared to the first game. The expansions, unfortunately, are pretty terrible.

The worst thing however, is that by buying this game, you are giving money to Atari, the impostor killers of the franchise. They dragged the RCT name through the mud and now the brand is relegated to horrible mobile games and the like. They at the very least let you still buy the actually good games - but it is like having to pay the man who murdered your grandfather for permission to visit your grandfather's old house.


OpenRCT2 is an open source fan project that fixes many of the problems of RCT, and [i]will[/i] fix that last one. If you have RCT2 installed, you get a vastly improved version of the original game. You get bugfixes, quality of life modern amenities, the ability to download scenarios from RCT 1 and custom scenarios. You get literal decades of fan custom scenery. You get multiplayer. You get improvements to scenario play.

What I've found the most fun with is the cheats unlocking immense potential in creative play, allowing you to make amazing fantasy and realistic builds in the game. There is a thriving OpenRCT2 creative community out there, with stuff like Deurklink Multiplayer and Head 2 Head on new element.

OpenRCT2  unlocks all of this and more, like several new official coasters like the hybrid and single rail, as well as new music. It's not too difficult to install either. There is no reason to play the original when you can play it significantly improved with OpenRCT2.

The cherry on top - it's still a good few years out, it's hard too gauge timelines on fan projects - but the ultimate goal of OpenRCT2 is, like OpenTTD, to eventually replace all the original game's assets with similar versions, enabling OpenRCT2 to be released for free, finally breaking from Atari's shackles.

So by all means, get RCT2, and then download OpenRCT2. You will not regret it.

I gave up basically because I couldn't play anymore when they switched to Wellbia. It got to the point where customer service required me to give Wellbia's CS permission to search my computer via remote access for the problem. This meant I had to leave my computer open to their use at a time that works for them, regardless of what I need to do, and it was also after going back and forth for about a week between both companies. 

I had thought one option would be that I could just play it on console instead, but because of how their account transfer system works...If I don't have access to my account on my PC, I won't have access to it on console. So I was kind of left with an ultimatum that just...didn't feel worth it for the amount of enjoyment and pestering for money I'd experienced with this game.  

I can't trade without paying premium. I can't have resonable inventory space or a way to manage items without paying for it. I can't even really use the market place without shelling out some cash. If I screw up my build, I have to pay money. If I want any particular cosmetic anything, I not only have to pay money, I have to get lucky in order to get what I want because of gachapon-gambling mechanics. And when this game inevitably sunsets and shuts down, I'm left with nothing but memories. 

Nah. PSO2NGS, I'm good. I think I'll stick to one-time pay games that don't require a breach of security all the way to the kernel level to play. At one time I thought it was good while it lasted, but...You've given me plenty of chances to take back that opinion.

review_text:
[i]Note: I want to thank Hastan for taking the time to respond to this review. This is a good developer who cares about making a game the community loves. As such, I will revisit this review as the game updates. It is my most sincere hope that I can change my review to positive in the near future.[/i] 

I really didn't want to leave a negative review because the demo had me so excited for this release, but I feel like I have to. In concept, its an arcade-style sports game (like NBA Street or NFL Blitz), combined with the charm of the old backyard sports games (Pablo 4ever), and with roguelite features mixed in. I love the game in concept... in execution it has flaws that are incredibly annoying. As such, I cannot recommend this game in its current state. It has to many bad design choices that make the game less fun.

Firstly, the more things you unlock, the less likely to get any one thing you have unlocked when you start a new run. You only get three choices. The result? You dilute your power and superstar pool with trash and have to start with things you don't want to play with. That is a punishment for unlocking things. Not a reward.

Here's a for instance: I unlocked a magnet power for 30 rubber [strike](which by the way, takes a long time to accumulate)[/strike]. I'd love to play with the magnet I spent all my rubber on, but 5 runs later it hasn't come up. So I spent 30 rubber on an item I don't actually get to use. That is an example of how roguelite features are treated in this game. They make the game less fun. If I unlock something you should let me pick it, especially if you are going to force me to grind currency to unlock it. Give me other incentives to play with the substandard powers and superstars but don't punish me for progress.

The most optimal strategy for playing this game would be, to spend all your rubber on improving McShaggy's stats early because you have to play with him every run. DO NOT pay rubber to unlock anything else until you figure out what you actually want to play with. Then once you've seen something in game that you think you would like to play with, spend rubber to unlock it. This is a perverse incentive, and it is not fun. Never unlock a bad superstar or bad power, because if you do, it will become part of your pool forever.

Other "features" that are not fun: 
1) I have rolled the same 3 superstars choices 4 runs in a row even though I have 6 available. That isn't fun. I want to try different superstars. 

2) The benchwarmers you start with are very bad, and they are given randomly.  You aren't going very far in a run where all your benchwarmers have sub 20 speed. They are too slow to handle the puck, and the CPU can easily skate around them when they are on defense. A player with sub-20 speed is basically unusable.

3) Why is the player goalie AI so terrible? Why is the goalie not upgradeable? I don't get to control him so it would be nice if I could make him better somehow. This problem is magnified by the simple fact that your goalie sucks and the other team's goalie is a god. It makes you feel like a slave to RNG. Yes, I know there are some events that affect your goalie, but they mostly just break him and make him worse. He can't pass at all. You are better off just covering the puck everytime and going to a faceoff.

4) Events are almost always more negative than positive. It is better to just avoid them... this is poor design. I understand the need for risk/reward, but the reward seems very low, which typically is a talent you could just pick up from the "score the first goal" game (and there you actually get a choice). The difference being that these "rewards" always come with a big stat hit or some other ailment that makes the player, on balance, worse. You also don't get to select who gets it. The game picks for you. Bad all around. Better off playing the talent game or going to the campfire and taking stats. This is almost always the case.

5) I don't want to post any spoilers but some of the later encounters have so much crap going on that they aren't fun. The enemy team just spamming superstar powers (because all 5 of them have them), while your stick flies out of your hand on every shot. Some of the powers are not avoidable. There were points in those games where my entire team was disabled in some way or another, and I literally didn't have a player I could control. I just got to watch the other team tee off on my goalie until they scored. Taking agency away from the player is not good game design. It didn't even feel like I was playing a hockey game in these encounters. I am not sure what it was, but it wasn't good. This needs to be fixed.

6) The hitbox for checking the CPU is inconsistent at best. If your players get breathed on they lose the puck. If they happen to actually get touched, they are down for what seems like an eternity. When you try to check? The other team frequently will just run right through you even when you have defensive talents and a high checking stat. 

7) Teammate AI is pretty awful. On defense your players just sort of collect in front of the net and stand there hoping to be hit with a puck. On offense they frequently get in your way instead of trying to find open ice where you can pass them the puck. Of all my complaints, I'd say this one is the least important. You can learn to play around bad teammate AI. You can even enjoy it if the rest of the game is good. The problem is, that I just don't feel like it is.

I really wanted to like this game. I hope the devs read this and address some of these items because I want to enjoy playing this game and I want this game to succeed. I think it could be amazing.

Edit: I have written some suggestions I believe would greatly improve the game.

My suggestions?

1) Allow the player to select whichever unlocked superstar power they want OR take a random unlocked power with a bonus.

2) Allow the player to select the Superstar teammate they want OR take a random + bonus.

3) Allow the player to have some impact on the benchwarmers they get. Whether its a choice of team style (speed, defensive, offensive) or select the individual benchwarmers from the bench warmer pool (this can be randomly determined). This ensures you don't get three players with sub-20 speed (I would argue that none of the players should have speed that low because it makes them completely useless).

4) Rework the second boss. It isn't fun or fair. Superstar powers need longer cooldowns. CPUs should not be able to off screen you with their powers. Certain powers should probably be removed completely (I am looking at you, block of ice).

[strike]5) Increase the number of rubbers the player receives from wins, and award a small amount in a loss.[/strike] The amount of rubber awarded was increased via patch. I no longer have any complaints about the amount of rubber awarded per run.

6) Do something with the goalie. Its literally your most important defender and integral to hockey and it is an afterthought in this game.

review_text:
Almost enjoyed it.  But too many systems are working against you.

Cons:
1- Only about half of the keys are remappable.  Which means the other half can't be remapped either because they overlap with the unremappable ones.  Why?!
2- The environment seems designed for close quarters.  There are very few places with sight lines.  This means you'll likely use your sniper rifle for in-close combat, since the other options aren't quiet.  Makes for not a fun sniping experience.
3- Enemies spend a LOT of time in cover when alerted.  This makes #2 especially bad since the lack of good sniping spots means you can't really reposition.  So, instead you sit and wait.
4- The character controller is sloppy.  It has too much inertia and reacts oddly to terrain that doesn't have scripted handholds.  You essentially feel like you're babysitting a drunkard as you navigate the terrain.

Pros:
1- Sniping feels good.  In fact, all the guns so far feel nice.  This part is really well done. Too bad the environment prevents the rifles from being fun.
2- The free-form objectives system is interesting.  Though the levels feel a little too closed-in for it to feel sandboxy.

Anyways... it feels like the team that was working on game mechanics might have said something that upset the team that did the environment design.  Because the latter almost feels purpose-built to sabotage the former.

review_text:
Left 4 Dead is a great game with a memorable cast of characters, unique mechanics that set it apart from other zombie shooters, entertaining and immersive levels, and addicting gameplay. Under any other circumstance, I would absolutely recommend buying it.

[b]However[/b], Left 4 Dead 2 makes the first game obsolete. It has [i]all[/i] of the content from Left 4 Dead, plus its own additional weapons, levels, enemies, modes. If you like the mechanics of the first game better, you can restore them using Mutations or Steam Workshop mods. Everything L4D can do, the sequel can do better.

The only reason to play the original Left 4 Dead now would be for achievement hunting or nostalgia value. I cannot recommend buying it except at a very low price on sale, and that's only if you are really curious about it. Buy Left 4 Dead 2 instead for the best way to experience the gameplay. For what it is worth, L4D is still a groundbreaking co-op shooter that is far superior to PvE games like Raid: WW2,

I was actually quite excited for this game when it was first announced but when the reviews dropped it instantly killed my hype, doubley so when dead space the remake came out to universal acclaim, and whilst I'm glad I've now finally played it I can safely say the reviews are right, this game isn't really that good despite some really nice graphics.

So before I start moaning too much I do want to say this is probably one of the best looking games I've played and it ran beautifully on my machine, the voice acting as well is really incredible and the overall presentation can't be denied, it's a shame the games world isn't really expanded on because it is presented in a fantastic way. I also can't really complain that this game is bad, it plays well, it runs well and looks incredible. It's one of those awkward games that is stuck on the edge of a thumbs up or down but ultimately I'm giving it a thumbs down.

I really didn't like a few things that being the combat, enemy design, story and atmosphere unfortunately that's the bulk of the game. 

The enemies are so uninspiring and bland that it really kills all tension the game has, the vast majority of time it'll be zombies...just zombies, when you have a cool sci-fi setting you can go crazy with awesome aliens or lovecraftian horror but no we get zombies, oh and a few enemies originally cut from dead space. 

Combat is so bad, it has some fun 3rd person shooting and completely rips off the Kinesis from dead space, the guns are very generic but they at least feel good to shoot, however the main bulk of this game is melee combat which in my honest opinion is just shit, it's spammy with no sense of skill and you are able to cheese it so easy by dodging. It's a system that was patched after launch because it just wasn't right and what we have now just feels so dumb because you just fight one enemy at a time, it really brings this game down and with ammo being so expensive it's a system you will constantly have to engage with. 

I won't spoil the story but have you seen aliens or are you aware of weyland yutani? Well then it's exactly what you expect, yano dead space was cool because it had the marker and cults and body horror and it was all in service to the genuinely interesting plot whilst this game, stuff just happens and it's all hand waved away at the end in one of the most tepid reveals I've experienced in a while. Is this the result of this game originally having ties to PUBG which they backtracked on late on development? Yeah probably but it sucks and the whole setting is wasted. 

I think for me the biggest deal breaker is that this game isn't scary and relies too heavily on cheap jumpscares which don't work and nostalgia from dead space, look at the end of the day if this game is going to spend 90% of the time reminding me of a better game and then 10% of the time annoying me then I'll just go play the better series. Not the worst game I've played and some will enjoy this a fair bit but for me a waste of potential.

Survival horror is a funny thing. Most well known survival horrors tend to provide you limited resources to handle any given problem. Navigating through a puzzle or fighting against a group of enemies often requires that you aren't wasteful because you're never sure when the next box of ammo, or the next healing item is at. And you really don't want an encounter where you're ill prepared.

Callisto Protocol's solution to handling survival horror is to give you an unbreakable electric bat, and a self recharging gravity glove that can pretty much kill anything you want instantly. 

I didn't hate my time playing it, and you might enjoy it too. Just don't take it seriously, and get it on sale. Clearly a lot of talent here that was wasted by terrible direction. Damn shame.

I know I don't have much playtime, as I literally just played through the tutorial, but I have posted a review on pretty much every SAO game on steam outside of IF so here are my first look thoughts:

1 - Combat feels good to use. It is a bit different from all of the other games, being most similar to that of IF. I may just not have played far enough, but it looks like the art chaining isn't in this one
2 - The game has a season pass. I haven't played enough to get an idea on how balanced it is.
3 - The game has LITERALLY Pre-launch Microtransactions... Sure, its all cosmetics, but even still... It looks like the currency you can get in game, but I haven't played far enough to know for sure.

This being said, these are all first looks in. Like I said, I just barely made it through the tutorial. 
- Gameplay feels great. 
- The Menu feels like it is based heavily off Free To Play FPS style games such as Halo Infinite and Splitgate.
- Several of the previous games Recollections and Memories are viewable in game. This includes Infinite Moment (Which isn't on steam), but does not include Last Recollection.
- Bonus items if you have Fatal Bullet. Maybe later other games will support this too.

Premium Edition:
I would not recommend getting this right now unless you REALLY want the artbook or Soundtrack. This being said, it does come with something not listed in the comparison chart - A survivors type minigame with Kirito. This can easily be beaten, and you can get every item and max them out in a single run. This costs an additional $40 at the time of writing, and while the soundtrack is great, and the art is cool, it is not worth the extra $40

Tl;Dr - If you like SAO, this game is a good one to play with friends. I would recommend waiting for a sale though, as I feel like it doesn't quite warrant $60.
