You're not gonna really notice it till you play the minigames and do some of the master trainings but when you do it really makes you wanna quit.

I love this franchise, with all my heart, but these remastereds have been a shlog to get through, 3 was horrid, 4 was ok and it probably was worse than I remembered but the fact it was better than 3 probably made me blind to it and 5 is just a mixture of amazing when fighting mooks but an absolute chore to fight fast bosses.

If possible, play the OG instead, it has worse translations but the game at least functions as intended. RGG really needs to step up with the polish on these lower budget titles cuz they're starting to get sloppy

review_text:
An impressive feat in quality and genre mixing!

At the time of this review the game is in early access and has had the Webgrave update released for just over 1 month. Review is subject to change depending on content added. 

The Story is very reminiscent of something like the Witcher while taking the approach of doing things in Fromsoft fashion with item descriptions and environment to tell the player the story which is a narrative style i do enjoy. There aren't really characters in this game except for notes but the game does a great job at focusing on the main goal rather than wasting time with exposition that would drag the experience down. 

The Settings are so well crafted and feel very lived in. I really like how each map that you can explore has many secrets that reward the player for exploration and dedication to leveling up and getting better at the game. Each zone within a map feels like a mini arena that offers a lot for players to explore and navigate during combat. It's very clear that the devs had a clear goal in mind and wanted to put out the best content that they possibly could. 

Visually, its gorgeous. Performance was solid for the most part with the newest map having some frame drops, but with this being early access and with the amount of updates and care that the devs give, this is only a minor hickup that will soon be fixed. Apart from that I didn't run into any bugs or glitches throughout my playtime. The Art Direction has this mix of both realism mixed in with a gothic aesthetic which i just love in games and definitely was one of the main selling points for me. It definitely feels very gritty which for a game like this is just the perfect vibe for the overall experience.

The Audio design is just so good as every weapon you wield feels like they pack a punch and even shooting enemies such as some of the armoured ones sounds great with the bullets hitting off metal. review_text:
TL;DR: Don´t buy at full price and you´ll have a nice four hours or so.

It´s a Giger-esque robot-porn-gore-walking sim with slight FPS elements, maze-like levels devoid of quality-of-life functions that can pride itself on style, graphics and atmosphere. 

It´s extremely immersive due to the lack of guidance, tutorials or intuitive UI. So yeah, this is how I would feel if I woke up on an alien planet, a job well done in that regard.
The playtime is - objectively, I dare say - a joke, you´re done after about four to five hours if you´re not running around like a total idiot (me) because you don´t know what to do or where to go.

Combat should be avoided, at least with the melée weapon which makes for a frustrating experience. I´m not sure if the game needed any combat at all or if this was more of an afterthougt to cater to the mainstream of FPS-gamers. On the other (heavily infected) hand, this game is anything but mainstream. 

There´s also no manual saves, no maps...this game not only doesn´t take your hand and prides itself in it but mangles each finger whilst laughing at you. Also it has no strong narrative (which again heavily adds to the unsettling style of the whole thing), no voice acting, tons of stuff one could consider disturbing if one were not totally indifferent towards violence, grotesqueness or macabre stuff in general (again, me). 

The ending is like a ruined orgasm after some hours of weird intercourse with a disturbingly beautiful person, leaving you with an unsatisfied "...why?!".
Than said person kicks you in your respective genitalia and shouts "Make up your own damn answers, that´s why!" before throwing you out. 
(You go play through chapter five without making everything about sex for at a least an hour!)

In the end, I might not be the target audience for this, but it was at least something special and not boring. Visuals and atmosphere are top shelf. So get it for maybe 10-20 and have some fun.

review_text:
A game I can't enjoy yet it is genius in multiple areas.
There's an era of gaming in the 90's where starting off in a horror scenario with little to no information as to why you're there that this game clearly emulates and does very well.
There are multiple plant and pay offs handled very well. This is the minor of minor spoilers but [spoiler] there is a section where you find a weapon that is also used as a key (essentially). You pick it up off a dead person. You later have a cinematic that leads you to the next area where you no longer have the weapon. You come across another area where a monster (and I'm being literal here) buries itself into your stomach and it's tail is the weapon you just had and just lost. The gap between these moments had no implication on the game at all, you never needed the weapon-key until this belly-creature attachment. But pulling it off a corpse means a whole lot more when you find out the creature in your belly is a life-draining parasite. [/spoiler]
It's small things like this that prove the creators of the game created and respected their lore and took it into account when designing it.

That being said...I don't like this game all that much. The combat is VERY scripted and frustrating at moments, trying to relive what some people found as "tension" in the original Resident Evil 4, where if it's difficult to maneuver you're more likely to panic and thus is a simulation in a horror theme. I've never found this to be effective because frustration and cheap deaths will destroy theming 100% of the time.
The puzzles are built around the protagonist's perspective, in other words all the mechanics of the machinery (loosely using that due to the bio-organic nature of it all) are as much of a mystery to him as it is to you. It's a nice touch at first, because it causes a curiosity to explore and try things out however it becomes clear quickly that the puzzles rely HEAVILY on the player's curiosity because in a game where your movement is very slow (even when running) the puzzles require you to walk back and forth repeatedly in the same level area before you can progress to the next, as if this was another element from the 90's gaming area it attempts to emulate (the dreaded back tracking of "what did I miss?")

In terms of appearance this game is drop-dead gorgeous. The animation of the environment and the...living(?) things in it is near-seamless. The lack of vibrant color allows for certain moments such as "emergency/science lights" to highlight what is important which proves they planned this seemless blend but knew it could cause confusion when on top of a limited exploration a video game can offer. In short, it's literally too beautiful for it's own good. There are times where it somehow breaks the science of reality and makes things seems desolate and claustrophobic at the same time.

However it relies on this a little too much due to the constant re-exploration the puzzles need and the multiple...so many cut-scenes. It handles transitions primarily in 1st person cut-scenes that quickly become annoying as EVERYTHING in this world takes it's sweet time - the protagonist included. The speed that he handles unlocking a door is insufferably slow, most likely in a similar attempt as the aforementioned slow = tension but it falls into the frustrating category fairly fast. Entering a door with a creature that's walking along the ceiling well out of your reach happens in a slow moving cut-scene where I guess the protagonist forgets how to walk because it takes literally 8 seconds for him to walk through it either to show how gorgeous it is and let the ambiance set the tone (which it was doing perfectly before you interrupted it thank you) and to show the creature moving away from you but it takes the entire ceiling in it's movement which is rapid and creepy, there's no way to possibly avoid it. The game relies on it's gorgeous art that it specifically places an immovable camera so you can see what's in it but this is another element that removes the horror aspect because if I was continuing to walk through and saw it move I'd react in game and not have the protection of a cut-scene. Which is hypocritical of me however...because this game loves these cut-scenes so much you can literally die in one. Without major spoilers here you can run through an entire level and succeed just to die in a cut-scene. 

Before ending in a brief summary another commendation this game deserves is Jouni Kalervo Havukainen and the In Slaughter Natives developed an exceptionally visceral, nostalgic, terrifying soundtrack. There is no quip here, it is simply remarkable and they deserve the love they are getting for this score.

In the end it's hard not to see my issue with the game as almost subjective and there is enough well-thought effort and execution in this game that has more love in it's design than most games today that I'm sure there are plenty who pick it up that will rightfully fall in love with it.
I will look forward to the next game this team releases.

review_text:
I'm honestly shocked to see this game rated as "overwhelmingly positive." I would say that for me, this one was a miserable slog. The story is token, but fine. Real trope-y. But, it's got a neat Kurosawa vibe that I really dig. It's fun enough. For me, 
though, the choices the devs made for the interface and gameplay loop are absolutely baffling. This is one of the few games I've ever played that I've disliked so much that I've decided to push through and beat it purely out of spite for the mechanics of it.

First off, it's marketed as a strategy game, but it is only a strategy game in the loosest sense. This is a puzzle game wrapped in an RTS interface. In a strategy game, as "strategy" is marketed in gaming, you plan your moves and react to the moves your opponent planned. In a puzzle game, you manipulate the environment and the actors in the environment to progress the game. In this game, you move several characters through what is basically a series of obstacle courses with a ninja theme. You need to use the tools your characters have to kill NPCs and manipulate the environment to get to the finish line. To me, this is no different from doing a sudoku puzzle; I would contrast this with, say, playing a game of chess or checkers or Total War: Shogun 2. There is nothing dynamic about your actions in this game: you are presented with a map full of NPCs and environmental cues, and if you to look hard enough at the clues and move your characters with just the right timing, eventually you'll beat the level. Is this necessarily bad? No. Not necessarily. I was disappointed that this isn't really an RTS or turn-based strategy game, but I was totally open to a puzzle game framed in a ninja obstacle course. And is there a strategy to puzzles? Yeah, sometimes. So is it pedantic for me to criticize this game for being a puzzle rather than a dynamic strategy game? Maybe. A puzzle game /can/ have strategic elements. But, the problem is, whether you call this game a ninja strategy game or a ninja puzzle game, Mimimi throws it all out the window with the gameplay loop. 

In my eyes, a strategy game has to have a gameplay loop that involves some combination of planning, action, reaction, and consequences. This game has a gameplay loop that involves "attempting" and "succeeding or reloading." There is no "react" option in this game. There is no planning for failures or reacting to failures. There is no "plan b." Why? Because you have unlimited quicksaves that you can use at any time, making this, essentially, 'save-scum' the game. If you plan poorly and get your characters killed, you have a reset button with unlimited uses. The devs did make mechanics for your characters getting "spotted" and alarms going off, but you will likely see this in-game once or twice at most, because you will quickload the second things go wrong. The second you get spotted, you'll time-warp back to before you got spotted, and adjust your "strategy" to accommodate whatever minute and obscure environmental factor it was that you didn't catch before. Any time you make any elaborate action with any character, you will be quicksaving at every mouse-click and loading the second it goes wrong. This is enforced by the fact that your game ends when any one character dies, and any character dies within two seconds of alerting the level's guards. 

It's... baffling to me why the devs would set up a decent game, great atmosphere, fun characters and character interactions (combining character skills is where the game shines), and then throw it all out the window by making save-scumming the core gameplay loop. If they had balanced their game's mechanics and fine-tuned the clunky interface, rather than promoting cheesing the gameplay, they could have had something really great. I'll point out that they include a slew of incredibly intricate achievements that you really would have to attack the puzzles with a strategic mindset to complete. "Beat the level without killing a guard" sort of things. But, the quicksaving is still a part of these achievements. Maybe if you play to nab all of these achievements, the game could be a challenging, strategic puzzle experience. But for myself, and, if achievement statistics are to be believed, most players, who beat every level pretty easily but are still frustrated with the clunky UI and still cheesing the character synergies to the extreme, it's a pretty mediocre experience.

If I had to sum it up, I'd say this game is the equivalent of doing a sudoku puzzle with a pencil rather than a pen. Fuck up? No worries- this ain't going on your permanent record. Just erase it and go back and look a little harder.

So.. I do recommended this game it does come with a slight warning - I do like this game, I had fun playing this game, I would say if you're one of the 5 people in the world who've been demanding more Ice Hockey games release on PC it's definitely one to buy. 

However, I do think this game has a serious Achilles heel that cannot be ignored and is holding the game back in a bad way: No Career/Franchise Mode.

Despite the game having great graphics, great physics, great gameplay and overall being very fun... it's painfully short, with those 2.8 hours on record I have already beaten the final team and 'completed the game'. I find the refusal to include a Franchise Mode baffling, especially for a Singleplayer only game.

I want to get hooked and go deep into seasons building a team or player, recruiting talent, watching them grow, dealing with the finances, having rival teams, or creating my own character starting as a young talent with potential and levelling them up over the seasons - it's the only reason I play sports games when I play those Offline but I cannot do that here and I feel that it's holding this game back.

It's fun and it's worth the money especially when it goes on sale, but I didn't hook me in for very long and I came away feeling very mixed - happy to have a good Ice Hockey game, frustrated that it doesn't fill the Career shaped hole EA Sports left when it became Console only.

review_text:
It's a good game. I first played it months ago, got confused, and gave up immediately.

After revisiting it and actually learning the basics, I've gotten a little bit hooked. What elevates this above other base building games is the scale of it. Each map is a small section of the whole world, and in order to play a new map you need to establish your colony enough to build a migration station and send some fellows over there. It's an interesting mechanic that adds a sense of longevity to your decisions. That also means your starting location is very important, a fact which unfortunately isn't highlighted very well.

A short while after starting a new map, corruption will start creeping in spawning enemy mobs that attack at night, which adds a bit of a tower defence element to the game. If you play smart and fast you can cut off and corner the corruption before it becomes a major threat, but this will cause it to spawn more enemies more often. If you don't want to deal with any of that the game does offer a peaceful mode with no enemies.

You also have a slew of God powers you can use, and you can grab and move around things like resources to help build and enemies to toss into death pits. It's a neat addition that adds in more direct control so you're not just sitting back watching everything happen all the time. Overall the game is pretty addictive, it's fun to see your little dudes working away and your base growing and expanding. I'm not sure how much diversity and variety in gameplay the different maps offer, as the two maps I played seemed fundamentally similar, but I've gotten like 60 hours out of it and I'm not ready to put it down yet. Worth.

review_text:
Rise to Ruins is an exceptional godlike village simulation game that blends the best elements of the god game management, tower defense, and city builder genres. With its similar feel to games like Rimworld and Dwarf Fortress, this indie game offers a unique and thrilling experience that will keep you engaged for hours on end.

The game has a pixel graphics style that is both charming and immersive. The attention to detail in the game's world-building is remarkable, and the game's environments are beautifully crafted. The game's soundtrack is also noteworthy, with a mix of ambient and orchestral music that perfectly captures the game's mood.

The gameplay in Rise to Ruins is harsh but satisfying. As a player, you take on the role of a god who must guide a small village through the dangers of a unforgiving world. You must manage your resources, build structures, and defend your village from hordes of monsters that threaten your survival. The game's tower defense elements are interesting, and the game's survival mechanics are challenging but fair.

One of the things that stand out about Rise to Ruins is the game's depth. There is a vast array of structures, technologies, and resources to manage, and each decision you make has consequences that affect the game's outcome. The game's sandbox elements allow for endless replayability.

Overall, Rise to Ruins is an outstanding game that offers a unique and immersive experience. It's a must-play for fans of the god game management, tower defense, and city building genres. If you're looking for a challenging and rewarding game that will keep you engaged for hours on end, Rise to Ruins is the game for you.

review_text:
One of the few good VR coop shooters around. The devs seem to be listening to community feedback and actively improving the game. Definitely worth the price, especially on sale. 5-6 hours to complete the missions on normal difficulty but the real game is on master and nightmare; better mods and a lot more enemies that require actual strategy and teamwork to survive. review_text:
Alright where do I even begin...
I think I should start by saying that if a walking simulator that heavily relies on atmosphere and environmental story telling with a bit of puzzling and first person shooting sprinkled here and there is something that seems boring/uninteresting to you then sadly this is not the game for you, However, if you truly look at and appreciate games as an art form then stick around, I have a couple things to say about this game.

You probably noticed right off the bat from either the screenshots or the trailers that this game is heavily inspired by the works of artist H.R. Giger (most famously known for being behind the visual design of the Alien movie franchise and specifically the famous Xenomorphs), for the uninitiated H.R. Giger's art style is known as "Biomechanical" - A fusion of human body imagery and organs with cold, metallic machinery that forms something... simply fascinating and awe-inspiring. I could just tell you that this game is basically an interactive art gallery where you just walk around and soak in the landscape, visuals, atmosphere and ambiance and call it a review but there's a little bit more to it than that.

For starters this game does NOT hold your hand in neither story telling nor world navigation and objectives, everything is left to the player to interpret what happened in the world you are currently inhabiting and what you should do next. the gameplay loop consists of 3 parts: Exploration, puzzles and combat.

For the exploration part, as mentioned above, you are left to your own devices to figure out where to go next and what you must do, there are no objective markers and no hints whatsoever which can be a turn off for some but personally it truly enhanced my immersion while playing this game. the environments are very dark and grotesque at first and at some points you'll feel like you're navigating the body of... something, with some structures resembling large organs in a familiar yet quite alien way which speaks volumes to how good the art direction in this game is. At a certain point the game's art direction really kicks into high gear as you explore what appears to be the ruins of a once great civilization and at that part of the game I literally spent no less than an hour just walking around and taking screenshots of every single thing in sight, to say my jaw hit the floor would be an understatement and the ambiance/soundtrack perfectly sets the mood as it shifts from being dark and foreboding in the darker early game areas to being grand and awe-inspiring later on and it just does a fantastic job in grounding you in your surrounding area.

 When it comes to puzzles they are kinda simple enough, nothing groundbreaking or anything you've never seen in a horror game before (although I would not necessarily call this a horror game unless you are squeamish or creeped out by gore) but when you do figure out the solution and it clicks it can be very satisfying as this game has excellent feedback to let you know you have completed what is expected of you without even saying a word.

And finally the combat, yeah this game is not exactly hard but not particularly easy either, you don't start doing combat until a little bit further into the game and even then it takes a while to get going but when it does it can be somewhat enjoyable even though it is slow-paced but it is the aim of this game after all. the enemy design is quite good and it will make your flesh crawl but sadly there is little variety in enemy types as I think there are like 4 or 5 enemy types, 1 of which is a boss that you'll only encounter in one area much later on. this is not a typical first person shooter so health and ammo refill stations are far and few between so sometimes it is best to just run past enemies rather than confront them and waste resources that you might need when running is not an option.

I was surprised by how long the game lasted tbh because I've heard a lot of people complain about how short this game and I guess that is true, however as I said above because I viewed this game as an interactive art gallery going into it I think the 9.6 hours i spent in this game is just perfect. You can probably finish it much faster than I did as I took my sweet time walking around basking in the atmosphere and taking screenshots but I feel like not taking your time to appreciate the effort put into this game's art direction is really missing the point.

Overall this was a very enjoyable experience and one that I think we need more of in the gaming world. I wouldn't say this is one of the best games I've ever played but its certainly been unique enough to peak my interest and keep me thinking about it for sometime and possible even revisit it in the future.

review_text:
Let me start off by saying that this is kind of a mixed review

The fact that there is a rogue lite game for hockey is so insane to me still, playing the game for the first time and seeing the creativity for the levels, individual  character perks, and  artefacts for the team is amazing. 


Played this game as a solo player experience and appreciated how it's not one of those roguelites where you don't have to play it twenty times before you can comfortably progress through the game, and after awhile started playing with friends who made the experience even better as there are many funny interactions in trying to communicate and strategize how to score against what seems to be the best blocker in the world. The enemies you go through are all pretty unique from each other with just  having different abilities, and the boss of each act is fantastic.

The upgrades, skills, and characters you can unlock with points you get through playing the game is also nice, but it can be quite of a grind to unlock them all, personally I didn't mind the grind you would need to buy everything. 


Now let me tell you why this is a mixed review, and why I even decided to type this. 

I love roguelite games, and getting every achievement in many games, so I am well known with unfortunate situations that may occur or just losing a run due to being a bad player, however what am I supposed to do when the enemy team shoots from across the field and scores because my goalie has to be the worst human alive. 


Honestly it's crazy to me how well programmed the opponents goalie is the way you can shoot 50 times at goal and get maybe 3-4 goals. Meanwhile the opponent shot across the stage for fun, just for laughs, my goalie doesn't move, doesn't attempt to block, and now i'm down a score because of this. The straw that broke the camels back for me had to be when (spoilers ahead for the first act boss) the ref who assist the team, grabbed the puck half screen, tossed it towards my goalie, and my goalie let it go for free. Currently working on the last achievement in the game, but this was so extremely frustrating because I feel like it's such a common occurrence. This game is amazing and the fact that a terrible goalie is usually what makes the experience horrible is such a shame, because it really is a great experience. I don't mind if they score because they shot it closely, made a trick pass shot, etc. But if I get scored on because they shot the puck at the slowest speed possible, and i visually see my goalie not do anything, I want to quit out so fast. 


Anyways this game is still an amazing experience if you can get past that and a great challenge, fun times as well with friends. I would still recommend playing this game, but just know you may or may not be speechless after a goal determines your run while you're learning the game

Jet Set Radio Future is one of my favorite games of all time and I beat it again recently on emulation.

Picked this up right after and it pays really good homage.

The jumping and rail connection isn't as perfect as JSRF but it's close and all the other mechanics make up for it. No having to refill spray cans, instead refilling fuel for boosters similar to jetpacks.

Being able to use rollerblades, a bike, or a skateboard is dope. Being able to run on foot is dope. The dancing is cool. The enemies aren't just copy paste. The story is also good. Music is not as iconic as JSRF but still good and especially a few tracks.

There are less areas but the ones available are larger and more detailed.

There is a significant amount of more graffiti options than in JSRF.

My only real con was the dream sequences. Those got old real fast.

All in all, I think it's a fantastic game and well worth the money.

9/10

I gotta say I toss and turn recommending this game, I love the story and truly hope that one day that can come out with a second game. With that said I wish they had taken more time to polish what makes this game so good and so different from others in the genre. This game feels GOOOOD when it works right, the hits feel solid, you feel the crunch of the impact when you send an enemy flying into a spiked wall, BUT what they failed to do was polish the games combat system. There are far too many moments where I died not due to playing badly, but do to moments where two enemies would swing at once and  the games UI doesn't understand trying to dodge that, so you attempt to dodge, only to find yourself being hit by the second person whom you can't dodge because the game has you stuck in an animation that you get ZERO I-Frames so they kill you every time, or at least injury you every time, which leads to combos of hits landing that never would have normally. So in that regard, when it was working correctly the games combat felt great. Only other note worth mentioning is that there is an enemy you face maybe 3 times in the whole game, and the main games mechanic is to get you used to using your melee weapon only to have this enemy 1 hit you anytime you try to do so, so hopefully you brought plenty of ammo because the game wont give you enough environmental bombs or objects to attack said enemy as well.

On to the story, THIS is what really kept me going, Jacob getting thrown in a prison that made no sense for him to be there immediately gave me chronic's of riddick vibes and I loved it, "death by tea cup" If you know you know ~.~ but the story progressed in a very steady and easy to keep up with manner that didn't leave me too lost, it in fact kept bringing me in for more. I have yet to purchase the dlc because I didn't know if after buying this game 3 years ago and never playing it, I didn't know if I would enjoy it enough to do so. I 100% will be getting the dlc after completing the game my first time through on Maximum Security, because I want MORRRRE, more lore to this awesome world they have created. I am leaving it this way as to not spoil anything for anyone. 

Overall I don't think I can say I would buy this game if it were 60$ unless you are a major fan of dead space and want something even harder, but expect bugs, expect a game that didn't get the love it should have. Otherwise, you should try this out when it's on sale, then for sure I would say it's worth the money.

review_text:
Buggy/poor scripting that disrupts game play experience. Terrible match-making. Rude, troll players (killers mostly). And a disrespectful community. Luckily, there are other multiplayer games out there that are a better use of your time and money. 

To put things into perspective for those interested, it took 9 years for the developers to realize that players didn't want to wait while being downed, so they added the "abandon" feature. Players now can leave when there's game play abuse. Before, a killer can down all four survivors and wait until they bleed out one-by-one. It's 4 minutes of dying state per survivor; all you do is crawl on the ground while hearing your avatar groan the same looping audio and killer chase music. Now imagine having that for multiple matches per session. 

Is that really an enjoyable game experience? And what about getting off hook and the killer is just outside hook range just to hook you again? Well, that's not fun - solo-queue or with friends. Anyone who complains about SWF (survivor with friends) doesn't understand that not everyone plays squad, and if they are, then its not on a regular basis.

I would have liked to play the original DBD when it was first released. The maps looked bigger, atmosphere moodier, and it was more about stealth. Sure, the game play experience was minimal and simple. But it felt closer to what the game was originally inspired by: the 80s horror/slasher films where killers are unrelentless pursuers and victims needing to hide and outwit with the fewest of meager resources. Really, who was one of the first licensed IP killers for this game? 

Now, DBD has transitioned into a confusing mess of an arcade game where you need a user manual to know what killer/survivors you are grouped with and what overpowered add-ons they have. The steep learning curve for survivors is so laughable that it makes total sense that most players main as killers in this game. It's almost always 1.5 percent bonus blood points for survivors.
 
Over the years, I wished for bigger/diverse maps and unique generators with different skill checks/challenges. After all, with each new survivor and killer for a chapter, you would expect further commitment towards holistic improvement of the game experience. Instead, I have seen corporate miscommunication, mile-long messages noting latest bug patches/kill switches, and unfulfilled promises. One can say that the game is for "casual" players, but that doesn't excuse it being downright unplayable at times. 

But what do I know? Maybe in this day and age, an obviously broken game can manipulate people to actually think it takes skill and mind games to win when it's easy for players to abuse the game play and ruin the fun. At the end of the day, there are no substantial preventive/counter measures towards ensuring fair play despite the so-called initiative for anti-slugging, anti-camping, and anti-tunneling that were made to address DBD's current rework. And by the way, afk killers don't get penalized but survivors do when they're afk? So a boring free win is acceptable and I get penalized for wanting to leave a stalling match? Am I missing something here?

There were moments when I enjoyed the game and its spooky campy vibes. There aren't a lot of multiplayer games in the horror genre which makes DBD one of the few. But this year, there weren't as many good moments. Yeah, let's all gather around the bonfire one more time and laugh about Jim the Pole, but the charm has faded and the air has gotten stale. 

Time for something new and properly tested.

What a fall for a studio that has been truly brilliant until now. The basic concept of the game is good and has some really appealing ideas, nothing less is expected from Stress Level Zero after all... but the execution... this time it didn't cut it for me.

The storytelling is quite disjointed, and although I didn't get very far into the main story, I had a constant sense of emptiness that would have been ignorable if it weren't for the technical aspects of the game (spoiler alert): it switches from moments of "rail-shooting" (literally sitting in a mining cart shooting fixed targets like an amusement park), to first-person go-kart tracks with a steering wheel that is so sensitive that it gave me motion sickness even though I am extremely used to VR, don't suffer from motion sickness, and have played numerous VR simulators of various types, including flight sims), to what was really the last straw for me: some sequences where you change "avatars" and find yourself in bodies that have proportions different from the human body, particularly in the length of the limbs, which makes even interacting with simple objects extremely strange, not to mention sheathing weapons and objects, which is already more complicated than in many other titles due to how the object anchor points have been calibrated.

I also found the movement and parkour much more "awkward", and I don't particularly like the fact that essentially every "level" is a timed course that is supposed to encourage you to climb the leaderboards.

I'm sorry but this time it didn't work for me, there are now much better titles out there and if you really want to do something in VR, I'll tell you: replay BoneWorks or jump into IntoTheRadius, personally I feel that depending on what you're looking for, you'll benefit in both cases.

I'll be keeping an eye out for any future updates

review_text:
I got this game free from a recent Humble Bundle and decided to try it out despite all the bad things I've heard of it.  Everything bad you've heard about this game is 100% deserved.  As a fan of Dead Space I wanted to give this a fair try so I completed the single player.  The first thing you'll notice is the combat is atrocious.  It is heavily melee focused and consists of doing the same dodge once or twice and then attack 3 times and repeat.  This is how every encounter goes for at least 3/4 of the game.  It gets very old very quick.

Performance for this game was decent on my system.  Likely since so many patches and fixes have been released since then.  The save system in this game is also garbage.  The only real "save" is when you get a checkpoint.  Anytime you do Save Game, it doesn't actually save the game and it even has some small text to tell you that.  Who thought that would be a good experience?  

The starter pistol is very weak and you get almost no ammo for it.  I played this on the Medium difficulty.  It's not until like half way or so through the game you actually start to get any other weapons.  The last weapon the Assault Rifle you don't get until the second to last chapter.  The best weapon I found was the Riot Shotgun, but even with the upgrades you still can't go around blasting everything.  

The story for the game also fell flat.  The pacing for which you're introduced to new characters and trying to build up characters is very quick.  Due to this I didn't care about any of the characters really.  There's no character development or anything you'd see in a good story.  What disappoints me the most is that there's elements in this game that I feel if done right, they could've actually made a great game.  The story in particular I feel they've got a really interesting concept that just wasn't hashed out correctly.  With so many wrong decisions it doomed the game from the start.

Starting with positives- the art style and general charm of the game is stellar. No complaints there- is a visually really cute game and the artists deserve praise for that.

I'll most definitely come back for the full release when the game is free to play- but for now I think the game is better off with people who can get hooked with it from the start. TLDR; beginning had a mental disconnect with me the player having played other looters before.

review_text:
The atmosphere and late game visual design is so good, but the experience is such a slog that it's hard to say it's worth it. Map aesthetics are a little hit and miss, with everything looking great, but throughout the short runtime each chapter takes up, they overstay their welcome. It makes the maps obnoxious to navigate. Not in a "surreal and disorienting" way, but because of dull repetition.
Geiger's work is grotesque and erotic. That's like, the whole deal. The game captures of of this in the last act, but most of the game is just the bio-mech gore. It's not bad so much as a lost opportunity.
The design gripes don't make the game unplayable though, it's pretty nice to walk around. Until you get interrupted by the puzzles or combat.
The puzzles are dull. The game launches with an obnoxious sliding block puzzle. There's the "rotate one piece and adjacent pieces rotate" flavor puzzle. Probably some others that I already forgot about minutes after finishing the game.
It's boring. It's not thematic. It's a sliding block puzzle except it's eggs.
The combat isn't any better. There's less than a dozen encoutners, and they revolve around slapping whatever you want to fight twice, and then turning a corner. The guns are a generic pistol and shotgun type weapon, which work fine, but you could remove all of the combat and have a sub-par puzzle game. Then you could remove the puzzles and have a pretty interesting walking sim.
The ending is really cool. Might even be worth going through the other 4 acts.... but also maybe not worth the time.

review_text:
This is a $40 game that I've sunk nearly 20 hours into in two days, and I'm going to love the next 20+ hours without a doubt.

This is a great game that knows what it is, what makes it great, and what brings a player back on day two and beyond. If you played destiny 2 and enjoyed it, you're going to love the gunplay here. 

There are also some really great design choices at play. For example, it feels great to have a large goal (your main objective) that you work towards in chunks (your runs) while pursuing smaller goals (individual gear quests).

To give at least one critique: some things aren't explained very well. This can push the player, albeit indirectly through frustration/misunderstanding, to look online to understand. You never want that in your game. For example, the duelist pistol passive (item interesting, description bad) or the vestal flame (no spoilers but the system is just dumped on you to figure out). However, that problem pales in comparison to how good and sleek the rest of the game is.

I'm looking forward to seeing what this game is like at full release and beyond-yes, I want multiple witch hunts on multiple fronts or countries. In the interim, there's more than enough to do for the price this game is at, by a wide margin.

review_text:
It's such a shame. 

BONEWORKS was one of the (if not THE) greatest VR games of all time. With how much I enjoyed the first game, and the clear passion that the developers had for IT, I was REALLY excited to see what happened with BONELAB after it was announced.
Let me say it again so it's clear; I LOVED BONEWORKS; this is not me hating both games.

It's BECAUSE I loved BONEWORKS as much as I did that this review hurts all the more.

Tdlr: BONELAB is a buggy mess with absolutely ZERO new ideas to separate it from it predecessor. 

While BONELAB technically does have "new" NPCs and Weapons, they're just either more machine guns, or buggy impact-free shotguns that simply aren't fun to handle.
NPC's are just reskinned Nullmen or Turrets. 

Half of the fun of the original BONEWORKS game was discovering this brand new world you were in, and trying to decipher what the goal of the protagonist actually was!
That's simply not present in BONELAB. You already know what this world is. You as a protagonist simply don't HAVE a goal. 
The new body-swap mechanic (on top of being buggy and broken as hell AND only being unlocked within the LAST HOUR of the game) isn't enough to make players feel like they're experiencing something new at all! It's just VR at different heights, something that VRChat, Chillout, and any VR game with custom characters has been doing for years.

There are two required driving sequences that are either a complete waste of time, being basically a mediocre roller coaster showcase you would have expected to see when VR was first commercially viable; or so ridiculously hard to control that you'll spend more time trying to reorient yourself and your stomach than you will actually driving.

It's clear that the developers had ideas and drive for BONELAB, but clearly not enough to warrant a "full" sequel, and especially not one that COSTS MORE THAN THE FIRST GAME.

Initially, people complained about the first game BONEWORKS; thinking that it was mainly just a tech demo. Obviously, this was wrong; as BONEWORKS actually contained an interesting story, new ideas/characters/USES FOR VR/PERSPECTIVE.
The same argument simply CANNOT be made for BONELAB. It's just BONEWORKS without a story, without new ideas, without interesting use of VR as a medium. BONELAB IS a tech demo of SLZ's new Marrow Engine capabilities. That's not enough for players.

If the game was around $20-25 CAD, I'd feel a little better about it. But, it's $45, which is more than BONEWORKS; and too much for how little there is.

I expected so much better from this game; and it simply couldn't deliver.

review_text:
First off, I want to say: I really, really wanted to like this game. Boneworks, as is known, was a huge leap forward for VR when it first released, and I still think that statement holds up today. It really felt like the first fully-realized VR shooter of full quality. A lot of that was due to how robust the campaign mode was; at first, the game felt like an experimental tech demo leaning on its fourth wall, but later on, you realize how much more the game has to offer. It was slow to reveal the full extent of its hand, and that really worked in its favor.
I mention this because Bonelabs is its opposite, in that way. It starts strong, interesting, intriguing - and then slowly but surely it becomes a glorified tech demo, but for real this time. And that's really sad to me, because it really seems like it should be the other way around. Boneworks, for all of its strong points, was still a highly experimental game that had areas in need of refinement. Climbing ledges occasionally proved impossible, ladders were painful, and the game generally hinged far too much on climbing that didn't feel all that great and left you at constant risk of falling and losing progress. Bonelabs, instead of trying to improve the physics of these interactions, just makes it so you barely have to do them at all. This was a perfect chance to refine the game to make interactions smoother, and they just... aren't. Janky as it was, and the addition of new bodytypes can actually exaggerate the problem. Bonelabs also feels very tech-demo in the sense that there's no real progression; you can find some of the better weapons in the game early on, and since all carried items stay on between loads, you can go through the entire game with the exact same set of weapons. Hell, later levels seem to have actively worse weapons, somehow. The usage of ammo as currency has also been completely removed, which makes it so you're never at any sort of scarcity or need to conserve. If you're not spraying every single room you enter three times over with machine pistols, you're never going to run out of anything. There is even a level in the [i]base campaign[/i] that has Sandbox mode's build gun directly in front of you when you start, which means that you can generate quite literally infinite ammo. Why even have limited ammo as a concept if it's barely used? This also makes it so that exploration feels a lot cheaper. There's precious few places where you're rewarded for finding a secret in a way that actually gives you something cool. There's not much TO explore, really, most of the campaign is completely linear. The only real thing you get as exploration rewards are capsules that let you have some toys in Sandbox mode, and I really could not care less about them.
That sums up a lot of the game, actually. The single player feels like it's just tacked on to a sandbox game. The game's new mechanic - switching bodies - is only put into the player's control at the very end of the game, and it's barely even needed there. The story of the first game was a little hard to work out, but it was interesting, and would've been perfect to explore further; and now, the story is barely even in the room, with a fuzzy non-ending that comes too soon and says nothing. The whole game just feels half-baked, which is just confusing, as it seems like there was so much to build off of. I wouldn't say I hated this game, I just desperately wish it could've been better.
(Edit! I've gotten into modding, which seems to be what SLZ was banking on with this game. MarrowSDK needs about double the amount of documentation that it has right now, and that's after 6 patches that also broke a lot of mods in the process. While we're at it, why did SLZ go through the effort to put in butt softbody physics, but not to put in any sort of third-person spectator camera? Why put in a feature that no one can even see, and why is that feature my cheeks? Aside from that, there's been minor tweaks to the main campaign to add some secrets, and ammo economy actually matters now that it's sort of a scoring system, but it still doesn't help the campaign's actual pacing.)

The story opens quite quickly showing you as a guy who is making medical drops from what I can gather and it directs your attention to a group that are apparently the cause to all the outbreaks and murders throughout space. One thing or another happens you go to drop off your cargo only to find your ship has been broken into and there is someone onboard, moving on and after crash landing on Black Iron Prison, Jacob is quickly taken into custody and arrested along with everyone else alive on board. 
The prison quickly goes to shit...Over the duration of the story most of the time your story is simply escape and survival but that all changes come chapter 4/5.

Callisto has some of the best gameplay Graphics I have seen to date and it is already almost 2 years old and it looks this good! My Rig isn't perfect but the best I could get out of this game is High on the graphical presets and it still looked amazing and didn't stutter much along the way.
All the lighting, Shadows, Smoke FX and sounds are all superb every piece of this game feels beautiful.
Jacobs model whilst doesn't retain blood and decay on his overalls or his suit, his body and head are always shown to be sweating when dealing with enemies or in a warmer environment, in the cold the sweat stops and your suit begins to freeze over as it should.

Callisto has many graphical settings allowing alot of optimisation however similar to Dead Space due to the 3rd person camera there isn't a FOV which is a shame as sometimes when ADS the camera is much too close and you can't see your surroundings well enough.
The Game comes with options to skip QTE's which is fantastic as I am here to play a game and during downtime I am here to watch and understand what is taking place on Callisto, not sit waiting to press some stupid buttons or I will die...

Callisto Combat - Oh boy the dreaded Melee I have heard so much about...what am I a fast reacting boxer XD This stuffs insane dodging left and right so I get some hammer hits in holy moly! 
Combat gets easier as you go on it is just a bit of a drag to think a stun baton does more damage than a gun. The gun can be used to extend melee combos though I don't fully understand the trigger for it as it happens less than often. It is amazing how quickly you can get your arse absolutely kicked, even sometimes 1 enemy can just wipe the floor with you simply because you lose rhythm when fighting or you miss a shot or instead of dodging the attack you block which still takes damage leading to an untimely death, this has happened to me several times and I don't see it as a fault in the combat I see it as a challenge to plan for more actively rather than thinking "this games piss easy" and then getting smirked. 
Healing mid combat is just an absolute no no, you cannot heal in time during combat EVER, the enemies are too aggressive and simply don't allow, every combat situation has to be assessed correctly and executed perfectly in order to not take damage. 
GRP replaces Kinesis from Dead Space and whilst I didn't use it too much if I ever did notice a spinning fan or a wall of spikes I would keep a open mind of where they are incase combat did end up happening so I could throw an enemy into these for a beautiful fatality.
There are many "joke" boxes on your linear travels where you think you're finding resources only to be jumped and ultimately get nothing for the box wasting 10/15 seconds of time for nothing after beating the 1st major boss in the mines this is when I noticed the boxes to become more troll.
The bosses are a learning curve, alot of the times the boss is a two-head but in different environments to make it harder but shoutout to the final boss, you were a mother fucker to beat, I had a ton of ammo and you still didn't die you motherfucker...It took some strategy to get around this one even on Medium difficulty, I dread to think what Maximum is gonna be like...

Callisto is rated as a Survival Horror but in my experience it felt more action based more than survival horror, the combat makes it so you have to decide if you wanna shoot an enemy or use melee, that's about all, oh and during the early game having only 6 item slot makes your life hell having to decide between cash, health or ammo. I chose cash personally so I could upgrade weapons to ultimately make the combat easier, however it seems to have made no difference I don't think...
Colletibles, I've had no issues with these so far, they are quite easy to find if you check every nook and cranny like I tend to do, there are a lot of roads that fork so you have to make a choice to go one way and hope it doesn't cause story progression and lock you out, in these cases I have found myself saving at the fork and running either way to check them out first so I don't lose the opportunity to find things completely and be forced to start a new game. The only issue I found was how each chapter shows a person of interest with a recording and key besides them along with a value like 1/4 or something which made me think how have I missed so much, having now completed the game it is basically telling you how many of that persons logs there are in the game.
Reforgers are fantastic little things, really highlighting how quick and easy it would be if everything could be 3D printed. This is basically your shops bread and butter, similar to Dead Space once again with a few design tweaks to come away a little different.
Lots and lots and lots and lots on vents to climb through and little gaps to squeeze through, I know this is a loading trick for todays modern tech but cmon, how many times am I gonna have to slow down because you wanted to make a game look fantastic and you couldn't get the game engine to handle at a reasonable level...just sayin'! I would rather doors and hatches be load oriented similar to Dead Space that these!


Sneaking sections, Now I don't mind a good sneaking section so long as it IS a sneaking section and not whatever this is, these enemies are "glued" to the walls until you pass them either by making sound or through contact. However during my efforts to stealth kill these fuckers all I found was sneaking up on them was impossible due to the fact that the second they spawn they know where you are, and the ones that are wandering the maps are moving so far ahead and squeezing through cracks that you then end up trying to catch them getting yourself caught by something else causing about 4/5 of these tentacle fuckers to be on your ass all at once. Not to mention when backtracking to check i'd been down all routes I could hear squelching noises from around me but I couldn't see nothing, bam 5 seconds later i'm being hit by a ghost...the enemy hadn't rendered somehow, fantastic!

Bosses are ridiculously over-tuned in this game even on normal difficulty, If you have no ammo you're basically fucked because melee does 0 damage to the final boss at least in my experience.

Overall I disagree with the reviewers and all the haters towards Callisto I thought it had a good story a beautiful set of Graphics and sound designs to go with it, the enemies whilst they aren't unique and are awfully similar to Dead Space it doesn't matter, the game was still a ton of fun to play and explore. I enjoyed almost every bit of my time on Callisto and for a price like £5 I couldn't pass up trying the base game!
9/10 from me.

review_text:
Witchfire, on the surface, seems like it should be a lot of fun. The idea of a PvE extraction shooter with the grit of a souls-like sounds really appealing! But in reality, this game just doesn't deliver a FUN experience, and ultimately, doesn't respect the time of the player.

This game has a serious issue with how it handles it's progressions, taking way to long to feel worthwhile, especially in the early game. There's no reason why I should be playing this single player game with the same starting loadout for 3 hours. It takes AGES to unlock anything new, being tied to 'Real Time' timers, which I'm sure is fine if you like to drown all your time into a single game, but for someone like me, it's frustratingly slow and unsatisfying. If any game that you play has the caveat that it gets better after "x" amount of hours, then it's just not a good game.

Witchfire also feels like it missing a core mechanic that all the souls games have (and the vast majority of extraction shooter for that matter), which is online gameplay. It's a lot easier to get lost in a game for hours on end when you've got a friend to play through with, but instead your slogging through the first couple areas by yourself while you wait for things to unlock. It just feels like a gaping hole in the gameplay, and with the developers staunchly against it, it feels like they're gimping themselves. Much like the souls games, I don't necessarily think it needs to be primarily a multiplayer game, but having the option of co-op would do the game a lot of good in the long run.

On a positive note, I think the visuals and atmosphere of this game are awesome. Artistically this game does everything right, from visuals to sound design. Theres a real gem of a game here, it's just buried under layers of unfortunate, un-fun decisions, and quite a few timers.

For some reason your first chicken coop, ranger hall, animal pen and kitchen can keep you going for a long while, up to 100 pop. The market is an option but it seems like there's only a limited amount you can import into your city. Now, without this problem there are no problems ... and that's a problem. The enemies are slow and attack one at a time. They need to group up and attack as a unit. Once you have the corruption contained, a few towers and a few golem spawns you're pretty well protected. They could attack any one of my towns with 10x the amount of forces that they are using and it wouldn't matter. I should be far more worried about the monster attacks than running out of food when I have so much invested in food production. I can't tell if its a glitch in the game mechanics but I've spent a lot of time on it and can not figure out why a hand full of buildings can feed 100 people and five times that many can't seem to feed more than 170. For $15 I feel like I got my money's worth (knowing me I probably bought it on sale) however after playing so much I have to say that after the first excitement of getting a city going the game is pretty boring. I guess I could just wait until the monsters get harder but the thought of that doesn't seem appealing.

Bottom line - Even though my first impressions weren't great I grew to really enjoy the game. I can see why people compare it to dwarf fortress, a challenging survival fantasy city management game with a terrible UI.

Ok, the UI is not as terrible as that but it is difficult. Sometimes the building options are in alphabetical order, sometimes they are grouped together by type and none of the buildings you might want to build first appear at the top of the list. Understanding this your best bet is to simple start a new game and take your time to read what every single build does, check out how the corrupt ground expands itself and prepare to dig in.

Build large fires to stop the growth of corrupted land, dissolve spell works for this also, have plenty of golems, and if you figure out why I can[t seem to harvest raw hides please let me know. LOL. 

The game has funny little glitches all over the place but when you think about the complexity of whats going on its completely forgivable. When I spell grab resources and drop them off to the villagers ... are they glitching out or in awe of my power?

Dead Signal seemed like I could make it through normal mode after beating casual without too much trouble, so I gave it a shot almost the entire day today. I KNOW there are more than enough events but often it feels tedious to search for them. Around 2-3 AM I find myself struggling and there is no way I will manage to find 10 events between 4 and 5 am when shit is hitting the fan enemy-wise.

Gave up trying, considering there is a chance even when meeting the quota to be very unlucky later on with one of the enemies and there goes my umphteenth playthrough.. Not complaining and I know the game is supposed to not be easy but at this point it's no longer for me. Anyways. still glad I played it and also looking forward WTTG3!

I just don't think I really see the point. There's potential here, but for someone like me who likes established characters to relate to and enjoy reading on and interacting with, it's hard to really see the point to anything in this game. 

Maybe playing it some more will change that for me.

review_text:
Scorn is a weird game, while I enjoyed the rollercoaster for what it was, I struggle to say Yes, you should play this. The answer rather is "No, unless"

Scorn as a game involves two main segments, a slow paced trek through a Gigerian Nightmare, solving puzzles and wondering if the sculpture on the wall is supposed to represent the fear of intercourse or the damaging effect of growing up and realizing your parents really did have sex. The art itself is very nice to look at but just a lot all around, the middle portion of the game particular being where you'll find yourself cross-eyed and forgetting whether the path with the phallic tendril going into the egg was the way you came from or the way you're supposed to go. The puzzles are alright, they're never too much of a head scratcher, and if you're struggling with one you just have to remember you only have to do it two more times. Every puzzle in this game adheres to the rule of 3's. Every. Single. One. Some areas have you spending minutes upon minutes walking back and forth up and down halls to repeat what you've done once and twice now.

The second segment of gameplay is combat, to make it short, the combat is not good. There are 3 Schlongs in this world, that you'll fight over and over. They'll despawn or stop attacking if you walk past certain thresholds in the map. The weapons never seem to have enough ammo, which results in encounters approaching tedium as your pistol runs out of spunk and there's always one more Weiner that you'll have to duke it out with the Melee Penetrator that comes with 2 hits and takes 5 seconds to use again after, and no, you cannot use the Penetrator 3 times if you take a week break between goes. There's a healing system that's just flat out not shown to you unless you open up the settings and look at the controls. There's an Organ constantly rearranging your insides that burns one of said heals every time he digs a little deeper. The saving grace of the combat is that it ends, jokes aside, you're only fighting off Todgers for a short 1 and half period of a 4-6 hour game.  Leave it to the Bollocks. Dong.

In short, if you can get past the mediocre gameplay and enjoy the art design for what it is, yes buy it but for most people there are 100 games that may not look as good. But you'll feel better after playing.

review_text:
Yakuza 4 was funny, with all the twists being as ridiculous as they were. Even though it had some pacing problems and tedious minigames, it still felt more compelling and motivating to play through than 5. 
Yakuza 5 feels like they completely forgot the epiphanies they made characters declare in 4. the ending also makes no sense and makes everything feel completely pointless.
There's no way to go through this other than every single chapter. 
I am going to spoil the entire game in this review.

Beginning with Kiryu's chapter, did anyone else feel excited when Kiryu left off four saying, "I'm the one who forced the tojo clan on you. Left you on your own. But now.. Im done running. Its time I take responsibility for my mistakes." only for his chapter to start... And he is a FUCKING TAXI DRIVER., in another city, pretending not to know Daigo or the Tojo clan?

It made me go wtf is he doing? and I was hoping they could explain this in a way that makes sense. But it doesn't because the game doesn't tie up loose ends from yakuza 4. I mean, holy shit, we see Kiryu with the Tojo at the end of 4, swearing in the saejima family and all; he jumped ship that fast?

This is all a part of Kiryu's internal conflict of not wanting to be involved with the yakuza because of his family. Yet, he involves himself in yakuza problems because he likes beating people up. I know everything Kiryu does in 5 is connected to how he can escape his fate as a yakuza, but Kiryu doesn't get close to solving this in this game.
In fact, at the end of the game, Kiryu ends up in the same situation as y1, 2, and 3. fighting some guy that wants to take over the tojo clan or something.

I started having a problem with Kiryu just because of this. He uses Daigo and everyone else in the tojo as cover for him until they can't cover for him anymore. He did that in the past games, but the nice part about 4 was him saying he'd stop doing that.
Well, he didn't stop doing that, and now he will go superhero mode again to fix everything.

Kiryu ACTS like he is some wise genius, but he doesn't think about his actions. He never takes responsibility. He only runs until he literally can't anymore. 
I wouldve been OK with this if they addressed how selfish Kiryu is and how he contradicted himself, but we get......
nothing
I would've liked the game 10x more if they developed Kiryu, but they make him go tojo superhero again. 
They also don't explain why Kiryu flipped the switch from his epiphany in yakuza 4. I get that it might've been because of Haruka pursuing being an idol, but I feel like it's different than that.
It just sucks when they build Kiryu up to be something to admire. Yeah, his physical strength is crazy but everything else? He is a disaster.

Very long Kiryu rant, but saejimas part is decent. It gets very dull in the last half, but his being in prison again is better than it was in 4. the nice part about his prison sequence is the people he meets; they are pretty interesting characters. Baba wasn't that bad either; they made a two-sided character that was good for once.
It is funny that saejima wants to make everyone his sworn brother. His parts made me appreciate him more as a character; even the showdown between him and majima were good. How he consoles other characters honestly to God makes him better than Kiryu. He is a genuinely good guy who doesn't fake his wisdom like Kiryu.

The fanbase of yakuza only cares about brawling mechanics, even though it steadily worsens from 3-5. Haruka's part of the story was a great breath of air. If I didn't have it, I would've suffered. They built up Haruka's character in this one, and it was great seeing her independent from Kiryu. It was also sweet seeing Haruka bond with the park. 

Park is one of the only exciting women characters in the series so far, as she is so ambitious. Seeing her try and be a mother figure for Haruka was great, and I liked that.
It started great, so that they couldn't have ruined it. Surprisingly they did! 
Park ends up telling her sob story, but it's a pretty good one. It made me respect her a lot more, except she introduces the central theme of yakuza 5... which is following your dreams.
She failed and couldn't follow her dream anymore, so she wants Haruka to pursue her dream. This wasn't a problem, but she got murdered for what we find out later, no reason. 
It's revealed that her ex-husband was majima, and majima wrote her a letter telling her he wanted to see her again??? 

So she was murdered for the letter, but they couldn't find it, and then they chased Haruka for it. They never get the letter, and it turns out that katsuya was best friends with park and didn't want her to die anyway.
While her death was an accident because of ogita, the entire majima letter plotline was stupid.. as the Osaka enterprise family and Kurosawa family go from desperately trying to get the letter to literally never mentioning or caring about it ever again by the end of Haruka's story. 

Then we have yet to receive confirmation from majima that he even wrote the letter, or why he wrote that letter... or anything. We get speculation from Akiyama and no epilogue resolving this part of the story. WHICH IS INSANE. YOUR TELLING ME MAJIMA DATED PARK WHEN SHE WAS LIKE 18 AN HE WAS IN HIS 30S, KNOCKED HER UP THEN SLAPPED HER WHEN SHE GOT AN ABORTION????? AN WE GET NOTHING MORE???

I liked Akiyama's part in the story, but he served to get Haruka's part over with. 
What was ridiculous was how everyone gave everything to ensure Haruka finished the park's dream of the japan dome; even Haruka wanted to do it! She was super stubborn and didn't want NOT to do it. But as soon as she saw Kiryu fighting on tv after the first song they performed, she instantly gave all of that up. 

Like, are you fucking kidding me???????? This just proved Park's point that Kiryu doesn't seem to let his kids be independent; they all rely on him. they genuinely do. Park was never cruel. She was telling the truth. While it's messed up for park to have projected herself so much on Haruka, she indisputably gave her lots of care and opportunity. 
But anyway, she gives up after everyone fights to keep Haruka on stage. So much for the main message being "pass your dreams onto others."

Then Haruka is running over the Kiryu as he's bleeding out... for the 3rd or 4th time in the series. That was incredibly disappointing to see. Especially when Haruka gave her speech, it was heartwarming until she said, "I can't keep singing!" like, are you for real? 
She had just left her role as the caretaker of the kiryus orphanage and the caretaker of Kiryu himself. Her character development seemed to be for nothing, all of everyone's sacrifices, for nothing. 

They could've had someone else rescue Kiryu instead of Haruka. If they had done that, it would've saved the entire ending. 

Overall the story had a lot of potential, but it didn't hit the mark. I would've been satisfied if they had made an epilogue that wrapped up some loose points.

review_text: I don't have enough good things to say about this game. I got it on a whim while it was on sale but it's 100% worth buying at full price (if that's in your budget). Challenging enough to keep me engaged, but not so difficult that I wanted to quit. And you can make it more difficult for yourself if you want, by playing on Difficult mode or trying to achieve some of the (very hard imho) optional objectives. The story is emotionally engaging, and the characters feel real (to the point that I got annoyed with some of them like I would real people lol). Each character has strengths and weaknesses, which influence how you can use them on each level. Every action has a consequence - if I set a trap *here* it will affect *this* set of guards, but how will the nearby civilians react? The art style is really attractive, the voice acting is top notch, and the soundtrack is phenomenal - the combination really transports you to the game's world. I played through the original game twice, the second time incorporating the Aiko's Choice expansion (which takes place in the middle of the original game), and I might dabble in a third playthrough one of these days, once my game backlog is a little better. If you like the challenge of strategizing an entire mission and overcoming all obstacles in your path, this game is for you!

I never played any game in the Phantasy Star series before. I was looking for a new MMO and decided to try out NGS despite the negative reviews since so many were comparing NGS to base, which I had never experienced so I figured I wouldn't really care about the differences. 

After about 10 hours or so, I grew bored of NGS. The story sucked and while the combat was cool and flashy, it felt like nothing was ever attacking back so not even the combat was fun. Not to mention, the game is pretty much dead. You'll see tons of people hanging out in the main city, but that's it. The second you walk out of the city, you'll never see another player. Also some of the players are just extremely weird. 

I gave up on NGS and decided to try out base PSO2 that everybody says was infinitely better. Not even an hour in and I fully understood why NGS is so hated. Base PSO2 has so much love put into it and there's so much character. Enemies actually feel dangerous and the bosses are some of the coolest in any MMO I have ever touched. Not to mention there's a CASINO!!! WHO DOESN'T LOVE GAMBLING?!?! Now this all sounds amazing and whatnot, however I quickly realized that I was extremely confused by the quests. There were story quests.. but they're all 30 second cutscenes? and each one just throws in some random character that you've never seen before who acts like you've known each other forever. And you can just select any of these "missions" whenever you please. Turns out Sega cut out the actual missions part and just left behind these random cutscenes without any context and the only other thing to do is exploration quests and urgent quests. Also one thing I always heard about the game was that there was several character concerts and I looked up where to find these. Yea, Sega cut those out of the game as well apparently. Thanks to NGS, Sega killed an amazing MMO that was like no other in favor of supporting the boring barbie dress up chatroom simulator that NGS is. I do still absolutely love base PSO2 and will continue to play it, but I'm still really upset that I can't experience the full game as it used to be and now my only hope is for private servers to release, but that'll only end up happening once Sega kills off all service to the game.

I love the atmosphere of games like this and mostly they are too hard. I have suffered at Darksouls and Elden Ring too much. The problem with those games is there was no (IMHO) reward for time served. The enemies were always hard no matter how often you played.

This game (for me) has the same aesthetic and while punishing is not frustratingly so. You can edge out into the evil world and run back to your base with spoils to grow stronger. Then venture out you go again. Not to say that will save you, it won't but it will help you. You can up the difficulty at your own pace through a Gnosis system and the tension is always real. Only to go to a new area and be destroyed, but that is part of the charm. Trying to get your dropped spoils (becuase you drop everything when you die) and rush back. I'm having a lot of fun and have only put my foot through the monitor and sent the Devs the bill three times.

The levels are gorgeous, the gun play fantastic. I like that there is no cut scenes or speech as it it adds to the whole creepiness of the game. Most fun I've had with a single player shooter in  a decade. love that it is single player. So very very very much recommended.

review_text:
I've purchased this AFTER I had played the demo for the next game from this developer: Shadow Gambit - The Cursed Crew. And I must say, I'm very disappointed. A lot of quality-of-life improvements are missing from this, making this title a slog. Examples: planning out coordinated strikes no longer stops time (and there's no real reason NOT to), you also cannot speed time up (if you need to wait for guards to move out of the way). Oh, and by default planned attacks use the slow walk speed, which is almost never desired.

The actual missions themselves are also "less fun", I feel. One needs to be a lot more careful and methodical to get anywhere without getting spotted and shot.

Also the voice acting is a bit… weird. The main characters are all fine and deliver their lines with a fun accent, befitting the setting… but then the guards themselves all speak without any accent, which feels a wee bit odd. I know, I’m nitpicking, but still. 

Perhaps had I not played the demo for Cursed Crew I'd find this a lot more endearing. But, alas, as is I’m just not having fun with this title and as such I cannot recommend it.

...I suppose I only have myself to blame - I played the Cursed Crew demo, saw this on sale and thought "oh, cool, this will be more of the same". I should have played the demo for this first, then my gripes would probably become apparent.
