review_text:
Scorn is a mixed bag.

PROS
+The game is beautiful in a disgusting way.
+The game is disturbing, just like it wants to be.


MIDDLE
- No dialogue and almost no text. This isn't something that breaks the game, but they didn't compensate for these limits elsewhere. Detailed below.



CONS
-The visual design for puzzles is terrible. It's hard to distinguish what is an interactable element or not. The worst is an egg puzzle early on that really, really doesn't explain itself. With no text or dialogue, visual design was even more important for a game with puzzles, but it feels like they made this part bad on purpose, to spite the player. The corridors also all look the same and it's very easy to get lost, especially during the puzzle underneath the big guy about 2/3 through.

-The storytelling is pretty mixed.

-The art-book is essential for understanding plot elements, but the digital version got downgraded after people had purchased it, which is one of the most consumer unfriendly decisions I've heard in a while.

-The save-points system is abysmal. Dying can send you way back and you have to go through a lot of nonsense to get back there.

-If you get behind on resources, like bullets or healing items, you are behind for the rest of the game. Missing a few shots is enough for this to happen.

-There is a lot of audio clutter, especially around the parasite that is on your back. Every hour or so, it screams at you, you look down and the parasite punches your guts. Also, this is unavoidable damage that can kill you, which is a terrible design choice and forced me to restart a chapter because healing is very limited.

-The boss fight takes way too long and is very repetitive, which is extra frustrating because of the previously mentioned check points garbage.


OVERALL
Scorn is a game that makes almost every decision against the player. It's a game that wants you to feel as much torment as the character you're playing as and expects you to like it. Scorn is a game that hates that it's a game and wants to watch the world burn.

review_text:
We have one Star Trek MMO.  It should be FAR, FAR, FAR better than this.  It's a tired game that never really gets better.  

You can do pretty much all of the content in a few days and after that, it's rinse and repeat.  They have various reps and currencies you can grind for but, to what end?  To redo the same very small amount of content?  

One would think worlds would be a big feature in a game about space travel and exploration?  Ground content is virtually non-existent, save for a few instanced encounters and those part of their small amount of story arcs.  You can land on planets, but it's a carbon copy of every other with some aesthetic changes here and there.  No chance of open world at all.

Even though it's F2P, they have insidious lockboxes all over the place forcing you to gamble real money if you'd like to acquire an iconic ship from the show you love.   Don't want to gamble?  Buy a ship with real money from their in-game store.  They offer 1-2 ships for in-game grinding once or twice a year, normally novelty non-cannon centric vessels.  If you speak to an STO apologist, they'll tell you you don't need to spend anything and you can grind X currency in game and convert it to Y - Yes you can in some cases, but takes you forever and the actions required to do it are the most tedious and mind numbing things ever.

I preordered this game, have a life time sub, and was waiting to login at midnight when they turned the servers on 10 years ago - I abandoned it shortly after logging in because it was awful.  

I came back after a few years (Legacy of Romulus 'expansion') and it did feel improved, spent a few weeks playing, realised it's an empty feeling and now login once every few months.  

What do most players do with this game?  Space Barbie (basically STO's transmog type thing) or Tweaking Ship Builds to knock up DPS numbers a fraction - DPS that is meaningless in a game that offers very little.

I will say that many of the ship designs are beautiful and it is the only game where you can pilot any number of Star Trek ships.  Pilot is a bit much though, it's micro-machines in space.

I pray one day a major studio will come along and the rights to this will be passed to them so we get a proper, 100% genuine MMO rather than this poor imitation.

review_text:
Had a good time with this one. Pathologic 2 is definitely an incredibly unique game with the way it's setup. I think something worth mentioning is that this game isn't for everyone as it can be incredibly punishing. With that being said, if you want an experience that will challenge you it's a great buy. 
   
   The gameplay pretty much comes down to a battle of resource management and decision making with timed pressure. The story progresses in a way where the clock is always ticking and regardless of what you do, will eventually reach the end. With this in mind you really can't afford to do everything on the map so you'll need to choose carefully. This is all the while keeping a close eye on your hunger, thirst and immunity meters as you navigate the plague running rampant. There were definitely a number of times where I struggled to keep things under control. Another interesting factor is that doing more isn't always better. You never know how certain interactions will influence the game state.
   
   I would say the most impressive thing about the game is the atmosphere. The soundtrack does a great job at keeping you on edge in the day to day. A lot of the character interactions can give the game a certain eerie vibe that really sold it further. The way the color palette and weather changes also contributes plenty. Overall I found myself highly immersed and liked this aspect of the game the most.
    
   If I were to make any criticisms it would be that hunger could stand to be just slightly more manageable (not too much, just a bit). It can be rather overwhelming to deal with sometimes so it might have been beneficial to tune the numbers to not be as intense while still not being easy. The other thing that comes to mind is performance. I have a high end GPU but still found the framerate to dip a lot with higher settings. With that being said, I don't think these things diminished my experience too much. It will be nice to see if Pathologic 3 can improve the technical foundation for more stable framerates.
     
   Overall I had a great experience with Pathologic 2 and will easy recommend it to anyone looking for a unique and also challenging experience. I don't think I've ever played something quite like it.

review_text:
I have many mixed feelings about Scorn. 

In many ways, I love it. It's a dark journey through a haunting nightmare realm, heavily inspired by the unsettling works of H.R. Giger and Zdzisław Beksiński. Every building and machine is a disgusting yet oddly beautiful amalgamation of technology and living flesh, and traversing the game feels like a biomechanical fever dream. The sound design is on point as well, from the sickly squelching of inserting a key to the muffled cries of a disfigured humanoid. Honestly, Scorn is one of the most visually and audibly distinct games I've ever played, and I applaud Ebb Software for creating something so unique.

However, the actual game-play of Scorn is... Not the best. There's no map, so it's easy to get lost in the labyrinth of hallways. Many of the puzzles are quite hard, and you can spend hours trying to solve them and never get anywhere. And don't get me started on the combat. Why do enemies take so much health? Why do you have so little ammo and healing items, and why are the refill stations single use only? I know survival horror is all about feeling helpless against horrific monsters, but there's a big difference between feeling helpless and actually being helpless.

All in all, I feel that while Scorn suffers from a lot of bad choices in game-play, it's a good start for a new studio. Ebb Software had a clear artistic vision, and they definitely achieved it. I would say that I high hopes for  this little Serbian game studio in the future, but unfortunately it seems like they've been shut down since November 2023, which is a damn shame, since I would have loved to see what they do next.

review_text:
Pathologic 2 is almost one of the richest and most interesting games I have ever played.
My experience playing the first few days was exactly what I never knew I wanted from an RPG. Days 1-6 felt like they stood on the edge of a knife. Constantly about to die from one thing or another, making tough decisions about what to do with my limited time and resources. Feeling like I would fall irreparably behind if I didn't work to understand every bit of information and game system. Utterly engrossing.
At some point I got the plague while scavenging a house on the brink of starving to death but I was sure I was nearly done making a cure. This was a prank so I spent hours and hours of game time completely locked in, making sure no opportunity slipped through my fingers, still barely clinging on. After investing the last of my borrowed time in making another prototype cure, my stomach and inventory were empty, my health was low and finding another sick person to serve as guinea pig would definitely kill me. I had no choice but to drink it myself, fully expecting it to give me some new horrible status condition and effectively soft-lock my current save. When instead I saw the infection bar recede and fully vanish I jumped out of my chair.
I wish I had stopped playing there though. I had a number of technical issues with the game. Framerate slowing to ~10 every 3 seconds even on min settings, several bugged out NPC interactions that obscured some of the later plot developments. One catastrophic bug occurred after getting fast traveled to the cathedral to meet with someone. That NPC spoke ominously about something about to happen, so I thought it was another world upending twist of the Pathologic knife when after this conversation every NPC appeared to have dialogue when I looked at them with my special eyes but then wouldn't talk to me. Curse of silence maybe? I wondered for HOURS how I was supposed to make any headway on understanding this ailment before googling out of frustration and realizing that it was a bug. And now I was going to have to load a save from the night before. After my first death the load screen told me I had 6 deaths, which at first I thought that was a really cool odd-ball story telling element that was going to be explained in one of the fourth wall breaking moments. Just a bug, which I only realized after finishing the game and trying to google its explanation.
More broadly though, even without those bugs I would not recommend you play the game. Not the whole thing anyway. The story starts to choke on itself in the second half. The characters of the town, who present so much intrigue on the first few days, are not that interesting on second inspection. They're all very well characterized, mostly as snooty and annoying, looking down on steppe-son Artemy and forcing you to toil in the gutter. But they're also completely useless. Even later characters who are made out to be powerful, imposing threats never do anything but stand there. Important people's houses are all weirdly partitioned so their state only effects a single self-contained zone. You start to feel like you're the only real thing alive in this paper-doll pantomime world. Ohhh man that was all intentional wasn't it; that's what the meta narrative was talking about the whole time! I wish it hadn't been. Maybe this kind of eyebrow waggling scanned a lot better around the release of the first game but once I started to see through the NPCs the world felt hollowed out and I was not interested in playing with the paper dolls for another 14 hours. It's honestly quite disappointing. I bought this game hoping for a Boneworks 2.0, but it's not. The Story is way too short (about 4hrs) and at least half of that time is spent solving cryptic puzzles and figuring out where to go next. If you want a fantasy combat arena game get Blade and Sorcery
If you want a military combat (arena) game get Onward, Pavlov or Hard Bullet
If you want a moddable VR Story game get Skyrim VR and install modpacks using Wabbajack to skip the process of modding for hours.

review_text:
Pathologic 2 is not a game that you play. It is a game that you go to war with. Unfortunately, your army is equipped with sticks and slings, whilst the enemy forces have fully automatic weapons and state of the art drones. In spite of this however, you are asked, not only to persevere, but succeed. This game was made by sadists who enjoy watching other people suffer - and it is glorious. 

Pathologic 2 is an oppressively difficult game, so much so that the developers actually had to add difficulty options post-launch due to public outcry, much to their own dissatisfaction as I understand it. If you play on the intended difficulty (and you should) you will find a game that kicks you while you are down and spits on your face. It is unforgiving and it relishes in that fact. When you die in this game, you are punished for it, you'll lose max health and max hunger bar which is very rough for a survival game. However, the difficulty of this game adds so much to the atmosphere that it makes the tension of the game almost palpable. There are other games out there that have world ending plots that aren't even a quarter as tense as this game is. This game will take you on a roller coaster of emotions. Most of those emotions will be stress-adjacent, but the ones that aren't are so powerful. This game offers a sense of earned-catharsis that rival and even surpass the Fromsoft games.

Dying in this game is very unforgiving and you SHOULD be afraid of death. However, you should be more afraid of giving up. This game has so much to offer and death is just part of the experience. You play as one of the few doctors in an eastern European town that is being relentlessly assaulted by plague, famine, crime and all manner of otherworldly things and it is your job to keep it together. Sound stressful? You don't know the half of it, because while you are doing that you also need to make sure to eat, sleep, drink, check up on people in town and be a doctor. In doing these duties, you will become engrossed in a unique world that is so different to anything that the current video game market has to offer. With excellent dialogue, endearing characters, solid survival game play and a fantastic atmosphere to tie it all together, I could not recommend this game more if I tried. If you're interested in a single-player, story driven, survival game with real consequences, play Pathologic 2. 

I know that this review is ambiguous, I have made it intentionally ambiguous, but I do not apologise for it. I went into this game almost entirely blind and I was treated to an experience that I will not forget, maybe ever.

"An open wound is a window into the world" - now go do your job as a surgeon and stitch it back up, Emshen.

review_text:
**Graphics and Visuals:**
One of the most significant improvements in PSO2: NGS is its graphics and visuals. The game boasts a more modern game engine and offers stunning open-world environments with impressive character models and special effects. The transition from the original PSO2 is remarkable, making for a visually appealing and immersive experience.

**Gameplay:**
PSO2: NGS retains the fast-paced and fluid action combat that fans of the franchise love. The addition of an open-world format gives players the freedom to explore, and the transition between combat and exploration is seamless. The introduction of a new class, the "Hunter," adds further variety to the gameplay, and players can expect intense boss battles and challenging encounters.

**Character Customization:**
The game continues to excel in character customization, allowing players to create unique avatars. There's an array of costumes, accessories, and hairstyles to make your character stand out, and the customization options are quite extensive.

**Story and Lore:**
While the PSO series isn't necessarily known for its deep storytelling, there's still an interesting lore and story to follow in NGS. The game expands on the existing PSO2 universe, offering more context and background to the world and its inhabitants.

**Free-to-Play Model:**
Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis follows a free-to-play model with microtransactions, and some players may find the monetization aspects to be a bit overwhelming or potentially pay-to-win, depending on their perspective. However, it's worth noting that the game offers a lot of content for free, and you can enjoy a fulfilling gaming experience without spending money.

**Community and Multiplayer:**
One of the strengths of the PSO series has always been its cooperative multiplayer aspect. NGS continues this tradition with engaging multiplayer content, and the game fosters a sense of community among players, encouraging teamwork in various activities.

**Updates and Content:**
One concern is that the game's long-term success may depend on how frequently Sega updates it with new content and addresses player feedback. At the time of my last knowledge update, Sega had been actively working on improving the game, but it's essential for the developer to maintain this commitment to keep players engaged.

Overall, from a gamer's perspective, Phantasy Star Online 2: New Genesis is a welcome and much-needed refresh of the beloved franchise. It offers improved visuals, retains the core gameplay that fans enjoy, and introduces an open-world element that adds depth to the experience. However, the long-term success of the game depends on how well Sega continues to support it and how it handles monetization. If you enjoy action RPGs, cooperative multiplayer, and character customization, NGS is definitely worth giving a try. [b] There is no point in playing PSO2:NGS. [/b]

 It's an "MMO" where even a peak hours there's probably a total of 1-2 people you see in 2-3 hours of free roaming, and they tend to ignore you anyways just like you'll eventually do to them. -Basically, a husk of an MMO with more AFK than playing.

 So how does it play, what if you wanted to play it as a singleplayer game? Well, it gets repetitive really quickly. Pick any playstyle and by the end you'll be mindlessly mashing buttons with a system that has the depth of a kiddie pool. It's like the devs are scared of players having fun with their builds, instead you conform to it because there's barely any variation in your choices. At least the movement is a little entertaining and fun at times, but that's about the only time I had my brain on, it's when I was exploring and not playing the main gameplay loop of beat up enemies while sometimes dodging, casting the same spells, and pressing buttons to win.

-Basically, Early Game is End Game, what you see is what you get.

 You can play dress up in this game. The choices you get are good (if you didn't pick a robot) and you generally have a lot of freedom. That's really good! So good that I see gooners and their eye sore porn addict characters. It's funny at first, but gets old fast. I made a really cool robot girl that actually took a lot of time, and I felt like I stood out like a sore thumb in the wave of big-breasted hookers, questionable characters, and the occasional fetish material. Why is this game so rampant with this?

-Basically, a Gooner's Paradise.

 Is the story worth it? Honestly, I couldn't tell you since I skipped it. 
-Basically, I skipped the boring story after 2 hours. No joke. There is nothing of value even when I didn't skip a cutscene late game, I wish I had. You might even skip this section when skimming over the review, just like how you'll eventually skip the cutscenes too!

 So would I recommend this? No, go play the original PSO2 instead. I'm not kidding, this was the biggest waste of my time and I needed some time to rethink my life choices. I haven't played this game in a bit but I assure you it's guaranteed to be the same even after a year of not playing, trust me. I waited! There won't be content coming to the game unless it's drip-fed additions that all play the same as always, repetitive and boring. Even locations in the game get old fast, and I love exploring! That's such a shame for the potential these spaces had, but there's nothing there except stupid collectable chests! I looked!!

-Basically, an almost empty map and an almost empty experience.

[b] TL;DR: Please either play PSO2 original (which has lots more depth and content, but I don't want this review to be TOO long) or any other singleplayer game, this MMO really does lack content like everyone says unfortunately, I don't see any reason to stick with this when many other games offer a unique and engaging experience that can stick with you for a long time, while this game slides away like grease, becoming a forgotten memory and a lifetime regret of wasted time that's forever linked to your profile. I lost nearly 66 hours of my life, please don't make the same mistake I did. [/b]

Bomb Rush Cyberfunk is a terrific game—from the world to the characters and especially the music. The game is a true callback to that early 2000s feel, and I love everything about it.

The gameplay is fun and engaging, and the combo system lets you experiment and find new ways to pull off huge combos. With the OST banging in your ears, that's all the motivation you’ll need. Surprisingly, the story is really good. Going into the game, I didn’t expect the story to take center stage, but it ended up being a huge factor in my engagement.

The only real downside is one of the activities in the story. The squad battles are fun and make sense within the narrative, but I just wish there was more variety. It’s always just about who gets the highest combo, and it's really easy to win.

If the complete game bundle is on a sale and you pay 20$ or Euros, you can purchase it.
If it's not on sale, keep your money.

The whole game is focused on melee, then they implement a "two headed" enemy who can be only killed with range weapons (or bugged). Smart game Idea you could think, but it's not. At least the game gives you ammo befor these 4 encounters start and they are in the last third of the game. Like one, after another, after another and then the end boss appears and the game ends.
This is where the DLC "Last Transmission" starts. It could have been possible to implement this DLC in the normal game and would be fine but not with this cash cow. In the DLC you get a new elee Weapon and your range attacks become more or less useless. This time you have to defeat new enemy types with melee, only another bad game design idea. The end boss of the DLC is the only enemy with a Health Bar shown to you. You can see how little dmg your "1 hit 1 kill" Hammer does on this enemy. Not sure why they implemented it, this DLC was more terrible with the forced "Hammertime" vs many enemys. You swing as fast as a snail and get hit. Maybe many ppl complained about the useless melee weapon vs "two head" in the original game and now they wanted to rage bait it with almost useless ranged weapons in the DLC.

This game took me 19,5 hours for two playthroughs on the highest difficulty. In the second run i skipped the cut scenes. The DLC took me 3,5 hours with like 30 minutes of try to kill 2 Robots in melee with my new Hammer friend. This was so interesting seeing how i combo 1 of the enemys while the other attacked me. After 3 Attacks i died from full health. That's what I call balanced or annoying.

I did not try the other modes but will try it.

The Story is okayish. I just don't understand where this "contagion" started. On "Eurpoa" or the Planet itself.
The DLC should have been a part of the main game from the beginning or be for free. The game ends and leaves you with a clif hanger. Stupid in my opinion.

The end game credits from the DLC are non existent but if you wait a couple of minutes you will get a funny cut scene.

I think this game was supposed to start a longer story. The Issue is that it will be burried after this DLC desaster. Cash Cow milking at it's finest.
60$ for the main game with only 12 hours playtime in the first playthrough is not ok!

The part with the blind enemys and "stab them in their back" was also pretty annoying in the main game. You kill 5 or more, the game spawns you 5 more in your face. Just because it can. If you alert on of them it's almost a reload.

You have the "grab and throw" thing whis can be usefl in the main game. You have plenty of "spikes" arounf you and can kill them that way pretty fast. The DLC didn't use this mechanic a lot. but it had "blades" you could grab an dthrow for a instant kill.

Long story short:
In my Opinion a possible purchase for 20 $/Euros in a sale for All contents of this game (like I did). Otherwise not worth the money and time. You can get a faster recap on Youtube and maybe there is a next game to this one which is worth the money from the start.

I would like to have a "neutral" Option with the Steam "Thumbs Up or Thumbs Down". Because for 20$ this would be a Neutral Thumb, for full price definetly Thumbs Down!

review_text:
Short Review: Strong story and worldbuilding, but boring gameplay.

Long Review:
.hack//G.U. is the 2007 continuation of the .hack series, introducing a new successor setting: The World R:2. Despite being a direct sequel to prior works, it does not require prior knowledge to fully enjoy -- in fact, I had only seen some episodes of .hack//SIGN in the mid 2000s before watching this. It is the first major series focusing on MMORPGs blurring the line between real and virtual worlds, about a decade before SAO did it. So how does it hold up?

The story is overall good, but the worldbuilding is absolutely fantastic. Your main drive is to save your friend who fell into a coma after being PK'd, and it's overall a treat for fans of MMORPGs. The story often comes in large chunks, with little bits put in around the end of minor quests. Throughout, however, you can check news feeds, six different forums, your emails, and even videos from ambush journalist Salvador Aihara to get a broader picture of what's happening around Haseo and the others. There is an immense amount of optional story that, especially in the first game, dwarfs the main story. These sources make this compilation a treat for people who enjoy story rich RPGs.

As for how the story compares to SAO? Despite similar themes, it's apples to oranges: .hack is like Star Wars while SAO is like Star Trek, because the former are Science Fantasy while the latter are Science Fiction. .hack has no grounding in the real world when it comes to any strange phenomena, involves religious concepts like AI deities and cosmic self-balancing, and ignores a lot of basic common sense when it comes to computing and hacking. SAO can mostly be explained in a realistic, near future scientific context. If you are fine with the mixing of the mystical with science, then you'll enjoy .hack.

The gameplay, however, is the weak link. The game's balance is absolutely atrocious. Levels make such an absurd difference that a 10 level difference can make the difference between one-shotting a foe or being one-shot. Item levels are virtually pointless -- I beat the second game with a mid-first game weapon at +5. Permanent stat upgrades are so overpowered that a migrated Haseo took no damage from mobs his level by the third game. Underleveled characters are fodder, especially with PKers whose levels center around Haseo's. The roguelike dungeons are lacking in features. The combat is oversimple and repetitive -- not even close to evolved as another, similar Namco series of Action RPGs: Tales. At a certain point I decided to just grind on dungeons 7 levels above Haseo and then curbstomp the story content.

The sound is a bit weird. The soundtrack is strong, leaning a bit on mysterious choral music. The English voices are a bit of a mixed bag. Atoli's voice is by far the strangest -- it may have been pitch altered at times and often sounds unnatural. Sound quality with voices also varies, suggesting that they weren't all recorded in the same studio. This seems to be cleaned up in the fourth game, as the voices sound crisper and Atoli sounds much more normal. The cast noticeably aged in that 10 year span, though.

I don't care about graphics, but they look nice. Clearly upgraded from 2007 standards so yay. Also, no apparent bugs from the conversion to widescreen.

Overall, it's best enjoyed by fans of story rich RPGs. The gameplay is shallow, but if this doesn't bother you, you'll like it.

review_text:
Everything I say here is only relevant once you get off the starting island as that is when the game "starts". 

My first impressions of the game are very positive, but things start to unravel a bit once you get a few hours into the game. The world design, the art direction and sound are immaculate, there is clearly a ton of work and passion here and I love it. The gunplay is satisfying, sending enemies flying with the stake gun is super fun. The little magic you have is often very powerful and will get you out of sticky situations. I do hope this game gets a multiplayer patch as I do think this game would be incredibly fun with friends. 

I want to like the game, but the difficulty spike once you unlock Gnosis I is actually insane. The difficult curve is non existent. I'd say wait until it has had some more time in the oven for the difficulty scaling to be reworked a bit. "Low" defenses has me dying on probably 60% of attempts. 

The combat pacing is also all over the place, even in low risk combat encounters you will find yourself quickly surrounded by 10 enemies. Sometimes an encounter will be a couple of enemies. Sometimes the regular encounters feel like highly dangerous encounters. The difficulty scaling just isn't quite there yet for me (though maybe I am just bad, I will accept that). When you combine 10 enemies that often do around 20% of your hp bar in damage, with only 2 starting heals (if you get lucky you will find another heal on the map, but often times its just poison mushrooms so it doesn't feel worth the gamble). 

While we are on the subject of difficulty tuning... the calamity events are summed up like this: how close to the extract portal are you? if you are not able to reach it in about 20 seconds your run is dead, and so are you (also the extraction portal is often surrounded by enemies with an elite or 2 tossed in there for good measure lol). 

I guess my next question is: why is healing tied to its own stat? I am not a fan of that choice personally. It is important to remember that leveling up increases the witch strength so... level up carefully. 

The game really wants you to unlock Gnosis as it dangles things in your face that require it, but as soon as you unlock it all hell breaks loose. Prior to unlocking Gnosis, I found the runs to be challenging, and often had me sweating but I could extract with my loot more often than not. 

If you are a glutton for self punishment then everything I have said can be viewed positively I suppose. 

I also find the roguelike elements during the runs to be of low impact, really the gear you bring into the run is the most important. So far I haven't had any rune pickups that changed how the run was going to be played. Save your money and time and just watch a play through.

What I liked:
atmosphere

What I did not like:
The developers are really really proud of their assets, so much so that you have to watch the animations play out every single time. Oh were you trying to figure out a puzzle and remembering what each piece does, get ready to be frustrated as every button makes you sit patiently while an animation plays out

Every puzzle was incredibly easy to logic out a solution but then I have to wait for the game so I can actually complete it, made the puzzles feel frustrating. Feels like things were added to inflate the playtime

why are there enemies? just because it's a videogame doesn't mean there needs to be enemies. Once again it feels like they were added to inflate playtime. 

I turned the game off after a desperate attempt to create tension by having an enemy inch forward as I was locked into a door opening animation, but at this point I know that things just happen in this game that I have no control over, I felt no tension just frustration as I calmly walked over and played the lamest rhythm game ever conceived of and "kill" the enemy

Went back and finished this """""g a m e""""" to everyone saying you don't have to engage with the regular enemies in this game, sure you can go afk while you wait for the monster to wander away, in fact not engaging with this masturbatory art piece would probably be a better experience. At some point in the developer's spray paint huffing session they thought they needed a boss fight to make it a game and added in what could almost be considered a puzzle boss but instead is just another lesson in how to frustrate your players. The "fight" is 3 sessions in a room where you need to break a homunculus from an 'egg' so you can put it into a hydraulic press, and the only way to break the egg is to put the homunculus into a robot body that wakes up and attacks you, and somehow the weapons you have are sufficient to fight the robot but not sufficient enough to break open the egg. This all comes together in the final sequence of the fight where because of plot you are unable to switch weapons or even reload leaving you with a 4 shot grenade launcher. So now instead of just fighting the boss like you did the previous times you have no access to any ammunition and have to hide from the boss until the convenient weak spot appears.

After all this is done you come to the final sequence of the game, which is when the developers introduce a new button to the game. In the final sequence you are swapping between bodies to solve the puzzle, and for the ONLY time in the game you use the spacebar to swap between bodies. 
I cannot stress how frustrating it is to be given a  unique prompt to perform an action at the end of the game only for that action to be mapped to a button that has not been used at all. I had to pause the game and look at the keyboard layout.

Do not buy this game, not even on sale, not even for $1. Honestly if you see this game in a bundle you are interested in just skip. Absolute waste of time and money

review_text:
I really wish I could like this game.  I remember enjoying it a bit when I first bought it, then I stopped playing.  Life got in the way, I didn't have as much time.

This game punishes you harshly for lack of knowledge.  If you do not understand exactly how all the game mechanics function, you will lose.  There is very little chance of learning your way to victory on the fly.  The tutorial gives random tips that help, a little, but I find that I've already figured out the (very basic) information provided by the time they appear.

The UI is awful.  Selecting villagers is an exercise in complete randomness.  Alerts will tell you when something happens with a particular villager, but good luck figuring out where.  Same thing with monster attacks and buildings being destroyed: these are important things, but figuring out where they are happening so you can respond is down to luck.  You must know what buildings you have where at all times or you will spend valuable time searching for the problem.  There are many spells that could be useful, but often they are dependent on timing and with so few ready spell slots you often have to go searching through a list of meaningless icons to find what you need.

There's also the issue of countering attacks.  There is no clear in-game way to tell which towers are effective against which enemies.  You can deduce, over time, that bow towers aren't effective against skeletons, almost everything will target a specter but few things actually do damage, and fire elementals are both tanky and will light everything - people, buildings, everything - on fire and set you back for days at a time.  Fire elementals have no effective counter I've found: probably keeping a magic tower up long enough to do some expensive upgrades would kill them faster, but since they can burn everything they'd just wipe out the tower in response.

There is no good source of all this missing information that I've found.  Bits and pieces are in various places, but otherwise you're on your own.  It's an exercise in frustration.

I really was excited for this game. I enjoyed the pre-release versions and had a good time, but was keen for full release with some more content and more importantly, improvements to the core mechanics.

Unfortunately it seems most of the problems with the gameplay have not been addressed. I feel like I am at war with the controls, constantly fighting missed inputs and poor hit boxes on objects I have clearly got my feet onto or over. These aren't massive issues in isolation, but combined together along with challenges that feel like they were designed on a build of the game without these problems it leads to frustration. And worse, once finally achieving the gold medal, no sense of accomplishment because you don't feel like you've overcome the intended challenge.

I do fully understand that this is a one man job and in that regard its very impressive. The reason I feel so disappointed is because it seemed like the game was improving incredibly well with each update through its early access phase. I do really hope that these issues can be addressed and improved with future updates. 

I don't necessarily NOT recommend this game as it runs very well, looks and sounds good, and scratches a parkour itch that often isn't scratched in this way in games. I am mainly voicing my disappointment and criticisms over the 1.0 release of the game.

review_text:
100+ hours and 100% steam achievements later, i am finally writing up this review!

i remember seeing criticism from someone saying that there isn’t a lot to do in-game, but i disagree. personally this is a game i can see myself coming back to, because while you might think “what now?” after completing the main (and technically optional) story quest, 1) there is still steam achievement completing you can do, and 2) i think a lot of the fun comes down to the amount of creativity/imagination you put in during your playthrough. i get super immersed while making up stories for my family and the other villagers. it’s fun to set goals for each season and each generation, and see what’s happening with the other family lineages at the same time.

things i like the most from the game:
[list]
[*]the art style! reminiscent of the paper mario series which i LOVE so there is probably some bias there. the hair and clothing options are very cute.
[*]the soundtrack is beautifulllll overall (except two particular tracks that gave me uneasy feelings, but i would adjust the music volume for them).
[*]the emote wheel which definitely added to the immersion: dancing with the other villagers at the winter gala, bopping for apples on halloween, expressing sadness and crying during funerals, sitting and enjoying nature in the forest while my child is foraging nearby, etc.
[*]the freedom to pretty much play how you want - having the ability to adjust certain gameplay settings is something i was super thankful for. i didn’t like having to stress over hunger and sleep so i toggled those off very early + adjusted to slow aging to really make my first playthrough enjoyable at the pacing i would prefer, no added pressure.
[*]the options allowed when it comes to children - pregnancy or adoption, and choosing who will be pregnant if it’s the former.
[*]the option to choose your clothing preference for weddings.
[*]the variety of traits and observing the different kinds of people that villagers turn out to be (…however i’m admittedly the kind of player to save before midnight and reload a day multiple times to make sure a villager gets positive traits + looks decent. i’ve death caked several cruel type villagers and wonder who that actually makes the cruel one… couldn’t be me right? ….nah) it’s interesting to see how different your game can play out from another player’s when we all start with the original lineup of villagers.
[/list]

things i didn’t like from the game:
[list]
[*]probably the biggest one: lack of a sorting feature for your storage/inventory. i think i read somewhere that they were looking into this, and hopefully it comes in a future update. for now though it makes organizing your stuff a daunting task.
[*]house decoration has several limitations. you can’t place things on top of rugs. and there is a particular bug where when you line up objects a certain way that creates some sort of invisible wall and it drives me INSANE. there are also some craftable items (like for crafting artisan items) that i wish we were given the option to place outside. it also would be nice to have some sort of option for the exterior of the house upgrades, but that’s not really a big deal.
[*]besides the bug mentioned above, the other bugs. there is one i think they’re working on fixing where your family just stands at the stairs - i’ve gotten used to it by now after playing for several in-game years but it is mildly annoying. there is another bug i’ve encountered at least once where the time randomly froze and i was unable to interact with things or save. this caused me to force restart and lose my day of progress which was quite frustrating, but at least it was only that day. another bug is the inaccurate baby happiness/hunger meter when you’re outside of your house. the bottle indicator to feed the baby also doesn’t show up for me sometimes - not sure why - but i resolve this by picking up the crib with the hammer and placing it down again, which resets their meter.
[*]the events do not come with clear instructions in game. [spoiler] it was a sad experience to show up to the harvest festival for the first time without having items prepared for the grange display because it didnt mention it beforehand in the invitation. [/spoiler] hopefully this may change in the future.
[*]some dialogue can be a little immersion-breaking, particularly when my children randomly start calling my character by their name instead of “mom” or the neutral word for parent.
[*]regarding the storyline, i do wish it delved a little deeper. [spoiler] learning more about limbo, timothy and your relationship with him, astra and her history, etc. would be pretty nice. it would be nice to know just a little bit more background about the original cast of villagers (besides the whitfields) but i understand that they're only there at the start. [/spoiler]
[/list]

overall, it’s a unique life sim that has a lot to offer and i would definitely recommend this game to friends. in spite of the cons listed, i’ve had a really fun experience playing so far, and right now i’m facing a dilemma of whether i want to continue my legacy after grinding all achievements or starting a fresh second playthrough. it’s also cool to see the active discord community and posts from the devs with what they’re working on. looking forward to future updates that may be added over time  ^^
